Und er sprach zu ihnen: Was ist das für ein Gespräch, das ihr miteinander führt, wenn ihr da geht und traurig seid? –Lukas 24,17.

Am 6. Juni 1944 landeten 156.000 amerikanische, britische und kanadische Truppen an einem 50 Meilen langen Küstenabschnitt der Normandie in Frankreich. Nach mehreren Monaten heftiger Kämpfe überwanden sie die anfänglichen Verteidigungslinien und strömten in das von den Deutschen gehaltene Gebiet. Der Überraschungsangriff, bekannt als D-Day, erwischte die Deutschen unvorbereitet. Erst im März des folgenden Jahres wurde Frankreich schließlich von den deutschen Streitkräften befreit. D-Day war der Anfang vom Ende des Zweiten Weltkriegs an der Westfront und das Ereignis, das scheinbar dem berüchtigten deutschen Heer die Lebensfähigkeit raubte, von der es sich nie wieder erholte. Es erscheint fast zufällig, dass so viele negativ konnotierte Wörter mit dem Buchstaben D beginnen: Enttäuschung, Zweifel, Traurigkeit, Untergang, Ernüchterung, Mutlosigkeit, Trostlosigkeit, Niederlage, Verzweiflung, Depression, Hoffnungslosigkeit, Verwüstung, Täuschung und Tod.

Ich kann mir vorstellen, dass diese beiden Gläubigen, die an jenem düsteren Abend den Weg nach Emmaus hinabstapften, sich ein wenig ähnlich fühlten. Ihr D-Day war völlig unerwartet gekommen. Ich vermute, dass jeder Mensch irgendwann Momente intensiver Traurigkeit erlebt hat – sozusagen seinen eigenen D-Day. Selbst manche Tiere haben bekanntlich eine melancholische Stimmung beim Tod ihres Herrn oder Gefährten gezeigt. Doch diese beiden Jünger schienen einen Schmerz zu erleben, der weit über den normalen Verlust eines Freundes hinausging. Sie starrten ins Angesicht der düsteren Realität, dass alle ihre hellen Hoffnungen auf ein strahlendes Morgen hoffnungslos zerschmettert am Fuß des Kreuzes lagen.

Dieses Leid war keine gewöhnliche Depression, sondern eine Depression, die mit einer Glaubenskrise verbunden war. Diese Art von Entmutigung ist ein Zustand intensiver geistlicher Qual, in dem der kämpfende, verzweifelte Gläubige das Gefühl hat, von Gott verlassen zu sein. Es ist ein hoffnungsloses Empfinden, dass die Sonne von Gottes Seligkeit verfinstert sei und die dunkle Nacht der Seele dauerhaft eingezogen habe.

Obwohl wir alle bemüht sind, solchen dunklen Versuchungen tapfer zu widerstehen, zeigt ein kurzer Blick in das Leben vieler gottesfürchtiger Männer, dass diese Versuchungen sehr real und recht verbreitet sind. In einem solchen Zustand erscheint das Leben unmöglich und die herabgesunkene Schwermut, die das Herz erfüllt hat, sieht kein Licht am Ende des Tunnels. Warum ist mein Schmerz ewig, und meine Wunde unheilbar, die sich nicht lassen will heilen? willst du denn ganz an mir sein wie ein Lugner, und wie Wasser, die verrinnen? –Jeremia 15,18. Dies ist offenkundig eine übertriebene Formulierung, die dem weinenden Propheten herausgerutscht ist, doch sie gibt uns einen unmittelbaren Blick in den gefürchteten Schmerz in den Tiefen seiner Seele.

Wir wollen euch, Brüder, nicht unbekannt lassen unser Leiden, das uns in Asien widerfahren ist, dass wir über Maßen gedrängt wurden, über Kräfte hinaus, so dass wir sogar des Lebens verzagt haben; vielmehr hatten wir den Beschluss, in uns selbst des Todes zu sein, damit wir nicht auf uns selbst vertrauen, sondern auf Gott, der die Toten auferweckt –2 Korinther 1,8-9. Diese dunkle Nacht der Seele macht vor niemandem halt. Sie dringt in das Leben von Fürsten und Armen, Predigern und Bußfertigen, öffentlichen und privaten Menschen, Kanzeln und Bänken. Diese beiden Jünger hatten auf dem Weg nach Emmaus bereits jede mögliche Szene noch einmal durchgesprochen. Sie hatten zweifellos sowohl bei anderen viel zu beanstanden als auch persönliche Reue empfunden. Die „Was wäre wenn“ und „Hätte ich doch nur“-Gedanken waren gründlich besprochen worden, aber nichts konnte das Ergebnis rückgängig machen und ihre unruhige Angst blieb bestehen.

Der Weg von Jerusalem nach Emmaus war etwa dreißig Stadien oder ungefähr sieben Meilen lang. Und auf dieser trostlosen Reise schloss sich einem verzweifelten Duo ein Fremder an in ihrem D-Day und fragte sie nach dem Grund ihrer Traurigkeit. Doch er ist kein neugieriger Zuschauer. Er ist der auferstandene Herr, der gekommen ist, um sein himmlisches Licht auf unseren verdunkelten Pfad zu werfen. Anstatt sich plötzlich zu offenbaren, und vielleicht zu unserem Nutzen, lässt er sie geduldig den erschöpften geistlichen Weg darlegen, den sie gegangen waren.

So entfaltet sich das Gespräch, während die Meilensteine vorüberziehen, und offenbaren jeweils unsere aufrichtigen, aber irrtümlichen Anstrengungen, die uns weiter von der Stadt des Friedens und tiefer in die dunkle Nacht der Seele führen…

…Die Unwissenheit anderer

Und einer von ihnen, mit Namen Kleopas, antwortete und sprach zu ihm: Bist du etwa der Einzige, der in Jerusalem fremd ist und die Dinge, die darin geschehen sind diese Tage, nicht erfahren hat? –Lukas 24,18. Frage irgendeinen Fremden auf den Straßen von New York, warum drei Tage nach dem Einsturz der Türme die Flaggen auf Halbmast wehten, und du würdest dieselbe ungläubige Antwort bekommen, wie sie diesen beiden zugeschrieben wird. „Wie kannst du so unwissend sein?“ Wir neigen dazu, uns über Menschen zu wundern, die nicht dasselbe Wissen besitzen, das wir uns selbst zuschreiben. Je jünger der Mensch, desto mehr Antworten glaubt er im Schatz seines Verstehens zu beherbergen.

Das ist nichts Neues. Mose, als junger Mann, …vermutete, sein Volk würde verstehen, dass Gott durch seine Hand ihnen helfen würde; sie aber verstanden nicht –Apostelgeschichte 7,25. Während er fest davon überzeugt war, den Plan Gottes in Händen zu halten, irrte er sich gewaltig in dem Maß, in dem er ihn besaß. Wenn unser Eingreifen die Lage nicht ändern kann, sind unsere Antworten nicht die wirkliche Lösung. Die herzliche Missbilligung, die natürlicherweise gegenüber denen entsteht, die anders sehen, ist ein erstes Zeichen dafür, dass wir auf dem falschen Weg sind. Meilen weiter auf dem Lebensweg begann Mose, die Verzweiflung dieses Schmerzes zu spüren und die Dunkelheit der Stunde. Ich vermag dieses Volk nicht allein zu tragen; es ist mir zu schwer. Und wenn du also mit mir umgehst, so töte mich doch, ich bitte dich, wenn ich Gnade gefunden habe vor deinen Augen; und lass mich nicht mein Elend sehen –4. Mose 11,14-15. Warum sah Mose das nicht früher im Leben? Aus demselben Grund nämlich, dass bei diesen beiden eifrigen Jüngern …ihre Augen gehalten waren, dass sie ihn nicht erkannten –Lukas 24,16.

…Vernunft

Er aber sprach zu ihnen: Was ist das? Sie aber sprachen zu ihm: Von Jesus von Nazareth, der ein Prophet gewesen ist, mächtig in Wort und Tat vor Gott und vor allem Volk –Lukas 24,19. Sie hatten ihre eigene Vorstellung davon, wer der Christus sei, aber sie sahen …durch einen Spiegel in einem Rätsel… –1. Korinther 13,12. Ihr teilweises Wissen stützte sich stark auf ihr eigenes Verstehen und suchte nach der falschen Art der Erlösung. Für sie war ihr Erlöser (in der Vergangenheit) ein Prophet, der nicht mehr das tun konnte, was sie von ihm wollten. Wir alle wollen, dass Jesus unsere Probleme löst und uns besser fühlen lässt, aber Sein Zweck ist es, uns von unserer Anmaßung und Sünde zu befreien.

Jakob hatte jeden Grund zu glauben, dass das Erstgeburtsrecht und der Segen ihm gehören würden. In Bethel hatte Gott ihm zugesagt, ihn zu segnen. Jakob erwartete, dass dies in materieller Form eintrifft. Und Jakob fasste einen Eid: Wenn Gott mit mir sein wird und mich behüten wird auf meinem Wege, auf dem ich gehe, und mir Brot zu essen und Kleidung zu geben wird, so dass ich wieder in Frieden zu meinem Vater komme, so wird der HERR mein Gott sein –1. Mose 28,20-21.

Doch der größte Segen, den er je von Gott empfing, kam zu ihm auf den Schwingen einer tiefen dunklen Nacht. Und Jakob blieb allein zurück; da rang ein Mann mit ihm bis an den Morgen. Und als er sah, dass er ihn nicht überwältigte, rührte er die Hüftwurzel Jakobs an; und die Hüftwurzel Jakobs wurde ausgerenkt, als er mit ihm rang. Und er sprach: Lass mich gehen; denn der Tag bricht an. Er aber sprach: Ich lasse dich nicht los, es sei denn, du segnest mich. Und er sprach zu ihm: Wie heißt du? Er sprach: Jakob. Und er sprach: Dein Name soll nicht mehr Jakob heißen, sondern Israel; denn du hast mit Gott und mit Menschen gekämpft und hast gesiegt –1. Mose 32,24-28.

Jakob hatte bereits einen Überfluss an irdischen Besitztümern angesammelt. Was hätte er noch mehr wollen können? Es war eine dunkle Nacht für Jakob, als er entdeckte, dass er sein Leben damit verbracht hatte, Besitz anzuhäufen und sich gegen Gott zu stellen. Nun sucht er gottesfürchtigen Charakter und geistlichen Reichtum. Sein Sieg kam durch Hingabe, und er hinkte fort, ein Lahmer mit einer Krone. Der Herr kann einen Menschen nicht vollends segnen, ehe er nicht zuerst seine Macht der Vernunft bezwungen hat.

…Unglückliches Schicksal

Und wie die Hohenpriester und unsere Obrigkeit ihn ausgeliefert und verurteilt haben zum Tode und gekreuzigt haben ihn –Lukas 24,20. Gott ist darin erfahren, ernste Verstrickungen in monumentale Siege zu verwandeln. Dennoch schaut der Mensch um sich und verflucht die Dunkelheit um ihn her. Obwohl ihnen manches Gute entgegenwirken mag, …ist der Morgen ihnen wie der Schatten des Todes… –Hiob 24,17. Dem Bösen um uns übermäßige Bedeutung beizumessen ist eine Verhöhnung der Göttlichkeit Gottes. Während wir alle zuweilen Dinge bereuen, die wir anders hätten tun oder sagen können, müssen wir die Ergebnisse doch unverrückbar in Gottes Hände legen. Hiob erlebte wohl mehr Unglück als mancher. So sehr, dass er …seinen Mund auftat und seinen Tag verfluchte. Und Hiob sagte: Verderbe der Tag, da ich geboren ward, und die Nacht, da es geheißen ward: Es ist ein Menschensohn empfangen. Möge jener Tag finster sein; möge Gott ihn nicht ansehen von oben, und möge das Licht nicht auf ihn leuchten. Mögen Finsternis und der Schatten des Todes ihn beflecken; möge eine Wolke über ihm wohnen; möge die Schwärze des Tages ihn erschrecken. Was die Nacht betrifft, so möge Finsternis sie ergreifen… –Hiob 3,1-6. Aber irgendwo, bevor die düsteren Ereignisse berichtigt und erhoben wurden, leuchtete das Licht in seine Seele, und er legte seine Hand an seinen Mund und betete an.

…Eigene Agenda

Wir aber hofften, dass er sei, der Israel erlösen sollte… –Lukas 24,21. Es ist nur natürlich, jede gegebene Situation begreifen zu wollen, und diese beiden hatten die richtige Gleichung gewählt. Ihr Fehltritt lag in der Annahme über die Mittel, durch die Christus dies vollbringen sollte, und über die Art der Erlösung, die sie erwarten durften. Sie sahen dem Tage entgegen, an dem ihre Nation über die Römer erhöht würde. Wenn wir unbewusst unsere eigene Sicherheit suchen, führt das zwangsläufig zu bitterer Enttäuschung. Naaman dachte …Er wird wohl herauskommen, zu mir stehen und den Namen des HERRN, seines Gottes, anrufen, und mit der Hand auf die Stätte schlagen, und den Aussätzigen heilen –2. Könige 5,11.

Abraham wurde das Land Kanaan verheißen und er bat um eine Bestätigung. Er bereitete das von Gott vorgeschriebene Bundesopfer vor, doch der ganze Tag verging, und Gott tat nichts mit ihnen. Und als die Sonne unterging, fiel ein tiefer Schlaf auf Abram; und siehe, ein Schrecken großer Finsternis fiel auf ihn –1. Mose 15,12.

Während Abraham auf Gott wartete, sein Opfer entgegenzunehmen, hielt er weiter die Raubvögel ab. Als sich der Tag dem Ende neigte, begann er sich von Gott verlassen zu fühlen, und die dunkle Nacht begann sich auf seine Seele zu legen. Es bedarf einer Mitternachtserfahrung, damit es dunkel genug wird, um die Sterne zu sehen und still genug, um seine Stimme zu hören. Wir aber hatten den Beschluss, in uns selbst des Todes zu sein, damit wir nicht auf uns selbst vertrauen, sondern auf Gott, der die Toten auferweckt –2 Korinther 1,9.

…Ungeduld

…Und außerdem: heute ist der dritte Tag, seitdem dies geschehen ist –Lukas 24,21. Viele von uns sind diszipliniert genug, eine Zeit lang auszuharren. Wenn aber unsere Hoffnung verzögert wird (siehe Sprüche 13,12), werden unsere Herzen krank und ermüden. Drei Tage schienen diesen beiden lang zu sein. Doch drei Tage, Wochen, Monate, Jahre oder gar Jahrzehnte liegen alle in Gottes Zeitmaß. Wie lange willst du mich vergessen, HERR? in Ewigkeit? wie lange verbirgst du dein Antlitz vor mir? –Psalm 13,1.

Josef ertrug geduldig die Misshandlungen durch seine Brüder und durch Potiphars Haus, doch der Kerker wurde lang, und er bat den Mundschenk, an ihn zu denken, wenn er wieder in seine Stellung eingesetzt würde. Doch es war volle zwei Jahre (1. Mose 41,1), bis der Pharao träumte und Josef schließlich hervorgeholt wurde. Aber es war nicht so sehr die Schuld des Mundschenks wie der Wille Gottes, der Josef berufen hatte, …in Eisen gelegt zu sein: Bis zu der Zeit, dass sein Wort kam; das Wort des HERRN hatte ihn geprüft –Psalm 105,18-19. Es gibt keinen wirksameren Weg, Geduld zu lehren, als die Zucht der Dunkelheit, von der wenige Heilige ausgenommen sind.

…Selbstmitleid

Ja, und einige Frauen von uns erstaunten uns, die früh am Grab waren. Und als sie seinen Leib nicht fanden, kamen sie und sagten, sie hätten auch eine Erscheinung von Engeln gesehen, die sagten, er lebe –Lukas 24,22-23. Niemand genießt es, etwas zu verpassen. Tatsächlich hat die Psychologie eine neue Störung entdeckt – FOMO (die Angst, etwas zu verpassen). Die Kunde, die die Frauen brachten, war eine gute Nachricht und eine erstaunliche Wendung, doch sie brachte den anderen keine Freude, weil es ihnen nicht widerfahren war. Gute Nachrichten dringen selten zu jemandem durch, der in Selbstmitleid versinkt; Elia war ein solcher. Seine dunkle Nacht kam nach einem atemberaubenden Triumph auf dem Berg Karmel gegen die Propheten Baals. Aber in der Schwärze seiner eigenen inneren Gefühle …bat er, dass er sterben möge; und er sprach: Es ist genug; nimm nun, HERR, meine Seele; denn ich bin nicht besser als meine Väter –1. Könige 19,4.

…Gefühl des Scheiterns

Und etliche von denen, die bei uns waren, gingen zum Grab und fanden es so, wie die Frauen gesagt hatten; aber ihn sahen sie nicht –Lukas 24,24. Es ist leicht zu denken: „Es hat bei ihnen funktioniert, aber bei mir klappt es nicht.“ Während missglückte Bemühungen uns entmutigen mögen, ist es nicht notwendigerweise ein Versagen unsererseits. Johannes der Täufer hatte das Volk zur Buße gerufen, Christus getauft und die donnernde Stimme vom Himmel bezeugt. Er kündigte den kommenden Messias zutreffend an und wies seine Jünger auf …das Lamm Gottes, das die Sünde der Welt wegnimmt –Johannes 1,29. Dieser Dienst verschaffte ihm einen sicheren Platz in einer dunklen Gefängniszelle. Er war an Mangel an Trost und karge Kost gewöhnt, aber es waren die Gefühle völliger Verlassenheit von Gott, die ihn in dunkle Zweifel führten. Und Johannes rief zwei seiner Jünger und sandte sie zu Jesus und ließ ihm fragen: Bist du der, der kommen soll, oder sollen wir einen andern erwarten? –Lukas 7,19.

„Lag ich falsch?“ In der Dunkelheit begann er, das Leben auf dem abfallenden Rücken eines Fragezeichens zu erleben. John Bunyan beschreibt es als den Sumpf der Verzweiflung. Es mag wie D-Day für den Christen aussehen, doch übermäßige Betonung unserer misslungenen Anstrengungen fördert keine Auferstehung.

Schlussfolgerung

Nicht alle geistliche Dunkelheit ist völlig vermeidbar. Nicht jede geistliche Erfahrung ist eine Zeit des innerlichen Segens, ebenso wenig jeder Ort. Es gibt Zeiten der Verfolgung und Prüfung, die dazu bestimmt sind, Heilige zur Seelenabrechnung zu bringen, die nur dunkle Nächte vermitteln können. Selbst Jesus wurde auf ähnliche Weise versucht wie wir, als in der alles durchdringenden Dunkelheit der neunten Stunde am Kreuz seine Stimme laut erklang: …mit einem lauten Schrei sprach er: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? das heißt: Mein Gott, mein Gott, warum hast du mich verlassen? –Matthäus 27,46.

Der Weg nach Emmaus bezeugt, dass ein lebendiges Glaubensleben keine Garantie für das Ausbleiben geistlicher Depression ist. Es ist eine Geschichte von echten Menschen mit echtem Glauben, die echte Prüfungen erleben. Es lehrt uns, dass selbst geistliche Freuden nicht zu festgehalten werden sollten. Unsere zuversichtlichen Visionen für die nahe und ferne Zukunft müssen in den Feuern der Demut getränkt werden. Die dunkle Nacht ist der Ort, an dem solche Selbsttäuschung stirbt und ein inniges Wissen um Gott geboren wird. Sie bringt uns dahin, Gott nicht mehr nur um der Gaben willen zu lieben, die er gibt, sondern Gott um seiner Beziehung zu uns und der Gemeinschaft mit ihm willen zu lieben.

Der Reisegefährte Kleopas’ wird niemals namentlich erwähnt. Manche meinen, es sei seine Frau gewesen. Andere behaupten, es sei Lukas gewesen. Doch ihre Identität wurde ausgelassen, vielleicht damit wir eher geneigt sind, die Lücke mit unserem eigenen Namen zu füllen. Sieben Meilen von Jerusalem entfernt stolpern wir über die schonungslose Erkenntnis, wer der Retter wirklich ist und dass Heil mehr ist als nur ein Stempel, der seinen Besitz kennzeichnet. Die Schuppen fallen von unseren Augen, und die dunkle Nacht der Seele weicht dem Glanz des hellen Mittagslichts der Gegenwart Gottes. Dann machen wir unseren freudigen Lauf zurück in die Stadt des Friedens, nur um wieder missverstanden zu werden. Und sie gingen hin und erzählten es denen übrigen; aber sie glaubten ihnen nicht –Markus 16,13.

Und so wundere ich mich sogar über die Ertragbarkeit, solche Gedanken niederzuschreiben. Es ist keine Begegnung, die man herstellen und intellektuell begreifen kann. Es ist eine höchst persönliche Zusammenkunft mit Gott und spezifisch auf jeden Einzelnen zugeschnitten. Doch vielleicht können wir in unserer oberflächlichen Generation ermutigt werden, der Dunkelheit entgegenzugehen und sie zu umarmen, anstatt ihr mit verachtendem Widerstand zu begegnen. Und dort, in der bedrohlichen Finsternis der Nacht, lernen, den Retter des Lichts zu umarmen.

Lang lag mein Geist gefangen da,
Fest gebunden in Sünde und Naturens Nacht.
Deines Auges Strahl war wie ein Lebenshauch,
Ich erwachte; das Verlies flammte auf mit Licht.
Meine Ketten fielen ab. Mein Herz war frei.
Ich stand auf, trat hinaus und folgte Dir.

- Charles Wesley

Around the world, but particularly in the United States, people seem to value rugged individualism. People who demonstrate this character quality make their own way through life, asking nothing from others and expecting nothing.

I suppose that this idea relates back to the pioneers. These were men and women who trekked across the various new countries looking for a place where they could settle down and call home. There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.

While this may sound like a scenario that demonstrates strength, the truth is somewhat different these days. These days people use technology to deliberately create bubbles of isolation around themselves.

Many older people have found themselves increasingly isolated from friends and family. COVID certainly made this worse, but there were seeds of this seclusion that had been sowed long before COVID was ever heard of.

Isolation is Not a Natural State

Looking back to the Garden of Eden we can see that Adam was created before Eve. While there were lots of animals around, there was no true companionship for Adam. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him … And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him –Genesis 2:18-20.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man –Genesis 2:21-22. Of course, this was the beginning of marriage, but the more important thing to see here is that it is not a normal state for humans to be alone. We desire companionship and not just the companionship of a pet dog or cat.

Isolation can lead to Despair

Perhaps there is no story that demonstrates so clearly the dangers of isolation as the story of Elijah. We know from the biblical book of I Kings, that Elijah was a fiery prophet of God.

He brought word from God to Ahab that there would be no rain and there was terrible drought for the next three and a half years. During that time, Elijah spent time in the wilderness and then with a widow in Zarephath.

The whole time, he was miraculously fed through God’s power, first by ravens and then through God’s provision of flour and oil to a widow, with whom he lived. Through God’s power, he raised the widow’s son to life.

Then came a time when he challenged the prophets of Baal to a match on Mt. Carmel and won a decisive victory for God. Miraculous fire descended from heaven in answer to his prayer. Truly, God was working great things in his life.

Very soon though, Elijah was running for his life into the desert. Jezebel had threatened his life and rather than trusting God, he fled to Mt. Horeb where he heard the voice of God.

When God asked him what he was doing there, Elijah replied, …I have been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away –1 Kings 19:10.

We can see here a big reason for Elijah’s weakness. He felt completely alone. God corrected Elijah’s incorrect assumption when He stated: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him –1 Kings 19:18.

The fact that those men and women existed in Israel did Elijah little good since he didn’t spend time with them. Elijah’s isolation led him to weakness and despair.

The story of Paul comes to mind as well. The Apostle Paul was a man who seemed to have nearly limitless amounts of energy and an unquenchable zeal for the things of God, but his last letter to Timothy from prison revealed a man who felt very alone. Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee… –2 Timothy 4:9-11.

The Apostle was not abandoned. Other than Demas, they had not fled because they were afraid or ashamed of his bonds. He had sent many of his friends away to strengthen the church in various parts of the Roman Empire. Yet, Paul was still feeling isolated and needed the good Christian brothers, Timothy and Mark, to come and encourage him as he faced a martyr’s death.

Isolation is Physically Harmful

Studies have showed that isolation is linked to higher rates of high blood pressure, heart disease, anxiety, and depression. Older people who are isolated often show signs of mental decline and can experience worsening dementia.

Many times, as people age, they experience the deaths of loved ones. The loss of a spouse can lead older people to withdraw from others and to experience loneliness and isolation. This in turn often leads to rapid progression of the aging process.

Science does not fully understand it, but loneliness leads to increased inflammation and poorer immune function. This in turn can lead to lonely people getting worse infections and struggling to recover after such an infection.

While we think of these problems as those that primarily affect elderly people, they can affect younger people as well. In younger people, often loneliness doesn’t lead to memory issues, but it certainly can lead to things like depression, and it can make chronic inflammatory diseases much worse.

The Opposite of Isolation

If asked what the opposite of isolation is most people would probably answer “Companionship” or maybe even “Friendship”. There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.

The Greek word translated fellowship in the New Testament is “Koinonia” and in the Bible it speaks of relationships that are founded on a shared love for God and for the church—a unity of belief and desire. Christian fellowship includes concepts like praying together, encouraging one another, and even suffering together.

I am afraid that many today find themselves in one of two dangerous situations. First, they may not be a member of any church congregation. While this may be unavoidable in certain mission outreach situations, it is not ideal, and most certainly it should not be a normal situation. At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed. We need fellowship, both to encourage us and to keep us accountable.

The second dangerous situation is that many believers, while members of a church, isolate themselves within that church. If you are a member of a large church congregation, it is easy to blend in and not develop relationships with others. This is just as harmful as not being a member of a church body. Too many people feel lonely, even when there are lots of people around.

Scripture makes it clear that we need a church body. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching –Hebrews 10:25.

There are many people who have lives that are full of friends and acquaintances, but if they do not have a place where they receive fellowship, they are missing out.

When I see people in my office who are struggling with depression there are two things I always tell them to do for themselves.

First is to start exercising. There have been several studies that compared exercise to antidepressants and found that it had similar effectiveness to many of the commonly prescribed antidepressant medications. This doesn’t have to be really vigorous exercise, but it does need to be aerobic (enough to raise the heart rate) and consistent.

The second is to become active in a church congregation; it is not enough to just attend church. Having brothers and sisters to pray for someone who is struggling, to listen to the discouraging situations, and to encourage that person to a more vibrant walk with God is really helpful.

Unfortunately, when someone is struggling with depression, the last thing they seem to want to do is make the effort to be around other people, which contrary to their feelings, is counterproductive to changing the problem.

As we consider this, it should move us to reach out to those who we know are struggling with isolation.

When someone loses a spouse, they often have a lot of encouragement for the first several weeks, but we need to make certain that they continue to have an active presence in their lives in the months that follow.

For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:5, should not give us excuse to not obey God’s command to Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2. The family of God is given no time limit on bearing burdens. There is only a mandate that as we see our brother or sister struggling, we are to help them, as we are able.

The blessing is that someday, when we are struggling, we will have men and women of faith around us to encourage us and to pray for us. We cannot carry these burdens alone. Together, we will reach the Celestial City.

Isolation comes for many reasons. Sometimes it seems to be a chosen way of life, as is the natural tendency of introverted people. Sometimes it is foisted upon a person due to deaths of loved ones or other significant losses. Either way, it is not a healthy place to live.

As we find ourselves in these situations, we need to reach out for fellowship. The family of God is there for us if we only reach out.

As we see others who are struggling, we need to extend to them the right arm of fellowship. As we do so, we may, through our small efforts, help someone emotionally, physically, and spiritually, simply by being a friend in a time of isolation.

في أنحاء العالم، وخصوصًا في الولايات المتحدة، يبدو أن الناس يقدّرون الفردية الصلبة. الأشخاص الذين يُظهرون هذه الصفة يصنعون طريقهم في الحياة بأنفسهم، لا يطلبون شيئًا من الآخرين ولا يتوقعون شيئًا.

أعتقد أن هذه الفكرة تعود إلى زمن الرواد. كانوا رجالًا ونساءً اجتازوا البلدان الجديدة المختلفة بحثًا عن مكان يستقرون فيه ويطلقون عليه اسم بيت. كانت المتاجر العامة قليلة وبقدر الإمكان عاشوا مكتفين ذاتيًا.

وربما يبدو هذا سيناريو يدل على القوة، لكن الحقيقة مختلفة إلى حد ما في هذه الأيام. اليوم يستخدم الناس التكنولوجيا خصيصًا لخلق فقاعات من العزلة حول أنفسهم.

وجد كثير من كبار السن أنفسهم معزولين بشكل متزايد عن الأصدقاء والعائلة. بالتأكيد جعلت جائحة كوفيد هذا أسوأ، لكن كانت هناك بذور لهذا الانعزال زرعت قبل أن يُسمع عن كوفيد بوقت طويل.

العزلة ليست حالة طبيعية

بالنظر إلى حديقة عدن نرى أن آدم خُلق قبل حواء. ومع أن الحيوانات كانت كثيرة، لم توجد رفقة حقيقية لآدم. وقال الرب الإله: ليس جيدًا أن يكون الإنسان وحده؛ أصنع له معينًا نظيره … وأعطى آدم أسماء كل البهائم وطيور السماء وكل وحوش الحقل، أما لنفس آدم فلم يوجد معين نظيره – سفر التكوين 2:18-20.

فأوقع الرب الإله نومًا عميقًا على آدم، فنام، فأخذ إحدى أضلعه، وسدّ اللحم مكانها. وصنع الضلع الذي أخذَه الرب الإله من الإنسان امرأة، وأتى بها إلى الرجل – سفر التكوين 2:21-22. بالطبع، كان هذا بداية الزواج، لكن الأمر الأكثر أهمية هنا هو أنه ليس من الطبيعي أن يكون البشر وحيدين. نحن نرغب في الصحبة وليس مجرد صحبة كلب أو قط أليف.

العزلة قد تؤدي إلى اليأس

ربما لا توجد قصة توضح مخاطر العزلة بقدر قصة إيليّا. نعلم من سفر الملوك الأول أن إيليا كان نبيًا حارًا من أجل الله.

أخبر أخاب بكلام من الله أنه لن يكون مطر فحدث جفاف رهيب لمدة ثلاث سنوات ونصف. خلال ذلك الوقت، قضى إيليا وقتًا في البرية ثم مع أرملة في صرفة.

طوال ذلك الوقت أطعمه الله بشكل معجزي، أولًا بواسطة الغربان ثم من خلال توفير الله للدقيق والزيت لامرأة أرملة كان يعيش معها. بقوة الله أقام ابن الأرملة من الموت.

ثم جاء وقت تحدى فيه أنبياء بعل على جبل الكرمل وفاز نصرًا حاسمًا لله. نزل نار معجزة من السماء استجابةً لصلاةه. حقًا، كان الله يعمل أمورًا عظيمة في حياته.

لكن قريبًا بدأ إيليا يهرب بحياته إلى الصحراء. قد هددته إيزابل بحياته وبدلًا من أن يثق بالله، هرب إلى جبل حوريب حيث سمع صوت الله.

عندما سأله الله ماذا يفعل هناك، أجاب إيليا: …فتفعلت غيظًا شديدًا للرب إله الجنود، لأن بني إسرائيل قد تركوا ميثاقك، وطرحوا مذابحك، وقتلوا أنبياءك بالسيف، وأنا أنا فقط بقيت، وهم يطلبون نفسي ليأخذوها – سفر الملوك الأول 19:10.

نرى هنا سببًا كبيرًا لضعف إيليا. لقد شعر بأنه وحيد تمامًا. صحّح الله افتراض إيليا الخاطئ عندما قال: وَلكِنّي بَقيتُ لنفسي سَبعة آلاف في إسرائيل، كلّ ركب لم تُنكب لبعل، ومن كلّ فم لم يقبّله – سفر الملوك الأول 19:18.

وجود هؤلاء الرجال والنساء في إسرائيل لم ينفع إيليا كثيرًا لأنه لم يقضِ وقتًا معهم. أدت عزلة إيليا إلى ضعفه ويأسه.

تخطر في بالي أيضًا قصة بولس. الرسول بولس كان رجلًا بدا وكأنه يملك كميات لا حدود لها من الطاقة وحماسًا لا يَطفأ لأمور الله، لكن رسالته الأخيرة إلى تيموثاوس من السجن كشفت عن رجل شعر بوحدة شديدة. سارع أن تأتي إليّ عاجلاً: لأن ديماس تركني محبًّا لهذا الدهر، ومضى إلى تُسالونيك، وكريسقنُس إلى غلاطية، وتيتوس إلى دَلْمَاطِيَّا. لوقا وحده معي. خذ مرقس وأحضره معك… – تيموثاوس الثانية 4:9-11.

لم يُتْرَك الرسول مهجورًا. باستثناء ديماس، لم يهربوا لأنهم خائفون أو خجلان من قيوده. لقد أرسل كثيرين من أصدقائه ليقوّوا الكنيسة في أجزاء مختلفة من الإمبراطورية الرومانية. ومع ذلك، كان بولس يشعر بالعزلة ويحتاج إلى تيموثاوس ومرقس، الإخوة المسيحيين الصالحين، ليأتيا ويشجعاَه وهو يواجه موت الشهادة.

العزلة مضرة جسديًا

أظهرت الدراسات أن العزلة مرتبطة بمعدلات أعلى من ضغط الدم، وأمراض القلب، والقلق، والاكتئاب. غالبًا ما يُظهر كبار السن المعزولون علامات تدهور عقلي وقد يزداد لديهم الخَرَف سوءًا.

في كثير من الأحيان، مع تقدم الناس في العمر، يواجهون وفاة أحبَّاءهم. يمكن أن يؤدي فقدان الزوج إلى انسحاب كبار السن من الآخرين والشعور بالوحدة والعزلة. وهذا بدوره غالبًا ما يؤدي إلى تسارع تقدم عملية الشيخوخة.

لا تفهم العلوم ذلك بالكامل، لكن الوحدة تفضي إلى زيادة الالتهاب وضعف وظيفة المناعة. وهذا بدوره قد يؤدي إلى إصابة العازلين بعدوى أسوأ وصعوبة في التعافي بعد مثل هذه العدوى.

بينما نتصور أن هذه المشاكل تؤثر أساسًا على المسنين، إلا أنها يمكن أن تؤثر على الشباب أيضًا. عند الشباب، غالبًا لا يؤدي الشعور بالوحدة إلى مشكلات في الذاكرة، لكنه بالتأكيد يمكن أن يؤدي إلى أشياء مثل الاكتئاب، ويمكن أن يجعل الأمراض الالتهابية المزمنة أسوأ بكثير.

عكس العزلة

لو سُئل معظم الناس ما هو عكس العزلة ربما يجيبون «الصحبة» أو ربما حتى «الصداقة». هناك كلمة أخرى ذات دلالة مسيحية أفضل من ذلك. تلك الكلمة هي الشركة.

الكلمة اليونانية المترجمة «شركة» في العهد الجديد هي «koinonia» وفي الكتاب المقدس تتحدث عن علاقات مؤسَّسة على محبة مشتركة لله وللكنيسة—وحدة في الإيمان والرغبة. تشمل الشركة المسيحية مفاهيم مثل الصلاة معًا، وتشجيع بعضنا بعضًا، وحتى المعاناة معًا.

أخشى أن كثيرين اليوم يجدون أنفسهم في واحدٍ من وضعين خطيرين. أولًا، قد لا يكونون أعضاء في أي جماعة كنسية. وقد يكون ذلك محتومًا في بعض أوضاع العمل التبشيرية، لكنه ليس مثاليًا، وبالتأكيد لا ينبغي أن يكون حالة عادية. على أقل تقدير يمكن أن يخلق شعورًا بالعزلة، وفي أسوأ الأحوال يعيق الكثير من مقاطع الكتاب المقدس التي تحث على «أن يَفعل بعضكم لبعض». نحن بحاجة إلى الشركة، لتشجيعنا وللحفاظ علينا مسؤوليًا.

الوضع الثاني الخطر هو أن كثيرًا من المؤمنين، مع أنهم أعضاء في كنيسة، يعزلون أنفسهم داخل تلك الكنيسة. إذا كنت عضوًا في جماعة كنسية كبيرة، فمن السهل أن تندمج ولا تطوّر علاقات مع الآخرين. هذا مُضر تمامًا مثل عدم كونك عضوًا في جسد كنسي. كثيرون يشعرون بالوحدة، حتى عندما يكون حولهم الكثير من الناس.

يُبيّن الكتاب المقدس أننا بحاجة إلى جسد كنسي. لا نهمل مجمعاتنا كما لبعضٍ عادة، بل نشجع بعضنا بعضًا؛ وبالقدر ما ترون اليوم يقترب – عبرانيين 10:25.

هناك كثيرون لهم حياة مليئة بالأصدقاء والمعارف، لكن إن لم يكن لديهم مكان يتلقون فيه الشركة، فإنهم محرومون.

عندما أرى أشخاصًا في مكتبي يكافحون الاكتئاب هناك أمران أقولهما دائمًا ليفعلوه لأنفسهم.

الأول هو أن يبدأوا بممارسة الرياضة. لقد كانت هناك عدة دراسات قارنت بين التمرين ومضادات الاكتئاب ووجدت أنه كان فعّالًا بشكل مشابه للعديد من أدوية الاكتئاب الشائعة. لا يجب أن يكون هذا تمرينًا عنيفًا جدًا، لكنه يحتاج إلى أن يكون هوائيًا (يكفي لرفع معدل ضربات القلب) وباستمرار.

الثاني هو أن يصبحوا ناشطين في جماعة كنسية؛ لا يكفي فقط حضور الكنيسة. وجود إخوة وأخوات يصلون لشخص يعاني، يستمعون إلى مواقفه المحبطة، ويشجعونه على مشي أكثر حيوية مع الله مفيد حقًا.

للأسف، عندما يعاني شخص من الاكتئاب، فإن آخر شيء يبدو أنه يرغب في فعله هو بذل جهد ليكون حول الآخرين، وهو عكس ما يساعد على حل المشكلة.

أثناء تفكيرنا في هذا، ينبغي أن يدفعنا ذلك إلى التواصل مع الذين نعلم أنهم يكافحون العزلة.

عندما يفقد شخص زوجًا أو زوجة، يحصل غالبًا على الكثير من التشجيع خلال الأسابيع الأولى، لكن يجب علينا أن نتأكد من استمرار وجود حضور فعّال لهم في حياتهم خلال الأشهر التالية.

لأن كل واحد سينقل حمله عنه – غلاطية 6:5، لا ينبغي أن يعطينا هذا عذرًا لعدم طاعة أمر الله أن احملوا أثقال بعضكم بعضًا، وهكذا تُكمَل شريعة المسيح – غلاطية 6:2. لا تُعطى عائلة الله حدًا زمنيًا في حمل الأثقال. هناك فقط فرض أنه كلما رأينا أخًا أو أختًا يكافحون، فنُعينهم قدر استطاعتنا.

البركة هي أنه ذات يوم، عندما نكافح نحن، سيكون حولنا رجال ونساء مؤمنون ليشجعونا ويصلّوا لأجلنا. لا يمكننا حمل هذه الأثقال وحدنا. معًا سنبلغ المدينة السماوية.

تأتي العزلة لأسباب كثيرة. أحيانًا يبدو أنها طريقة حياة مختارة، كما هو الميل الطبيعي للانطوائيين. وأحيانًا تُفرض على الإنسان بسبب وفاة أحبَّاء أو خسائر مهمة أخرى. في كلتا الحالتين، ليست مكانًا صحيًا للعيش.

عندما نجد أنفسنا في هذه الأوضاع، نحتاج إلى طلب الشركة. عائلة الله موجودة لنا إن بَسَطنا يدنا فقط.

عندما نرى الآخرين يكافحون، نحتاج أن نمد لهم ذراع الشركة. بفعل ذلك، قد نساعد شخصًا عاطفيًا وجسديًا وروحيًا من خلال جهودنا الصغيرة، ببساطة بكوننا صديقًا في وقت العزلة.

And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

E disse loro: Che discorsi sono questi fra voi, mentre camminate, e siete tristi? –Luca 24:17.

Il 6 giugno 1944, 156.000 soldati americani, britannici e canadesi sbarcarono su un tratto di costa di 50 miglia in Normandia, Francia. Dopo alcuni mesi di combattimenti intensi, superarono le difese iniziali e si riversarono nel territorio occupato dai tedeschi. L'attacco a sorpresa, noto come D-Day, colse i tedeschi di sorpresa. Tuttavia, non fu che nel marzo dell'anno successivo che la Francia fu finalmente liberata dalle forze tedesche. Il D-Day fu l'inizio della fine della Seconda guerra mondiale sul fronte occidentale ed fu l'evento che sembrò prosciugare la vita dal temuto esercito tedesco, dal quale non si ripresero mai più. Appare piuttosto coincidente che così tante parole con una connotazione negativa comincino con la lettera D: Disappunto, Dubbio, Dolente, Destino funesto, Disillusione, Scoraggiamento, Tetri, Sconfitta, Disperazione, Depressione, Disperazione, Devastazione, Inganno e Morte.

Posso immaginare che questi due credenti, trascinandosi lungo la strada per Emmaus quella sera cupa e triste, si sentissero un po' allo stesso modo. Il loro D-Day era arrivato del tutto inaspettato. Sospetto che ogni persona viva abbia almeno una volta sperimentato momenti di intensa tristezza—il proprio D-Day, per così dire. Anche alcuni animali sono noti per esprimere uno stato malinconico alla morte del padrone o del compagno. Ma questi due discepoli parevano provare un dolore ben oltre la normale perdita di un amico. Stavano guardando in faccia la cruda realtà che tutte le loro luminose speranze di un domani radioso erano irrimediabilmente infrante in un cumulo rovinoso ai piedi della croce.

Questa agonia non era un'ordinaria crisi depressiva, bensì una depressione legata a una crisi di fede. Questo tipo di scoraggiamento è uno stato di intensa angoscia spirituale in cui il credente che lotta e disperato sente di essere abbandonato da Dio. È un sentimento di speranza svanita, come se il sole della benedizione di Dio fosse stato eclissato e la notte oscura dell'anima fosse diventata una dimora permanente all'interno.

Mentre tutti noi cerchiamo valorosamente di resistere a queste oscure tentazioni, una breve ricerca nelle vite di molti uomini pii rivelerà che queste tentazioni sono molto reali e abbastanza comuni all'uomo. In tale condizione, la vita sembra impossibile e la cupezza che si è posata sul cuore non scorge luce alla fine del tunnel. Perché il mio dolore è durato sempre, e la mia ferita è senza rimedio, che non vuol guarire? Vuoi tu essermi del tutto quale un bugiardo, e come acque che falliscono? –Geremia 15:18. Questo è ovviamente un'esagerazione sfuggita alle labbra del profeta in pianto, ma ci dà un'istantanea diretta del temuto dolore nelle profondità della sua anima.

Non vogliamo, fratelli, che ignoriate la tribolazione che ci venne in Asia, come fummo oppressi altamente e al di sopra delle forze, così che disperammo perfino della vita; anzi avemmo dentro di noi la sentenza di morte, affinché non confidassimo in noi stessi, ma in Dio che risuscita i morti –2 Corinzi 1:8-9. Questa notte oscura dell'anima non fa distinzione di persone. Invade la vita dei principi e dei poveri, dei predicatori e dei penitenti, dei pubblici e dei privati, dei pulpiti e delle panche. Questi due discepoli avevano verbalmente riesaminato ogni possibile scenario nel loro cammino lungo la via di Emmaus. Non avrebbero di certo mancato di trovare molte colpe negli altri oltre al rimorso personale. I «e se» e gli «ah se solo» erano stati discussi a fondo, ma nulla poteva invertire l'esito e la loro ansia inquieta rimaneva ancora.

La strada da Gerusalemme a Emmaus era circa sessanta stadi o approssimativamente sette miglia. E lungo questo cupo viaggio uno Straniero si unì agli sventurati compagni nel loro D-Day e chiese loro conto della loro tristezza. Ma egli non è un curioso spettatore. Egli è il Signore risorto che è venuto a gettare la Sua luce celeste sul nostro sentiero oscurato. Piuttosto che rivelarsi bruscamente, e forse per il nostro beneficio, egli pazientemente permette loro di esporre la strada spirituale svuotata sulla quale stavano camminando.

Così la conversazione si dipana mentre i punti di riferimento delle miglia passano, ognuno rivelando i nostri sinceri sforzi errati che ci conducono più lontano dalla città della pace e nella notte oscura dell'anima…

…L'ignoranza degli altri

Uno di loro, che si chiamava Cleopa, rispose e gli disse: Sei tu il solo a esser forestiero a Gerusalemme, e non sai le cose che sono avvenute in questi giorni? –Luca 24:18. Chiedi a qualsiasi estraneo per le strade di New York perché le bandiere sventolavano a mezz'asta tre giorni dopo che le torri caddero l'11 settembre, e riceveresti la stessa risposta incredula attribuita a questi due. «Come puoi essere così ignorante?» Tendiamo tutti a meravigliarci di persone che non posseggono la stessa conoscenza che immaginiamo di possedere noi. Più l'uomo è giovane, più risposte crede che i forzieri della sua comprensione contengano.

Non è cosa nuova. Mosè, da giovane, …pensava che i suoi fratelli avrebbero capito come Dio per mezzo delle sue mani avrebbe liberato loro; ma non lo capirono –Atti 7:25. Pur essendo convinto di possedere il piano di Dio, si sbagliava gravemente nella percentuale che possedeva. Se il nostro ricorso non può rettificare la situazione data, le nostre risposte non sono la vera risposta. Il disprezzo sentito che naturalmente nasce verso coloro che la pensano diversamente è il segnale iniziale che siamo sulla strada sbagliata. A molti chilometri lungo il sentiero della vita, Mosè cominciò a sentire la disperazione di quel dolore e l'oscurità dell'ora. Non posso portare io solo questo popolo, perché è troppo gravoso per me. E se tu fai così con me, allora ammazzami, ti prego, se ho trovato grazia ai tuoi occhi; e non vedere la mia miseria –Numeri 11:14-15. Perché Mosè non vide questo prima nella vita? Per la stessa ragione per cui gli occhi di questi due ferventi discepoli …eran tenuti che non dovessero conoscerlo –Luca 24:16.

…La ragione

E disse loro: Quali cose? Ed essi gli dissero: Di Gesù di Nazareth, che fu un profeta potente in parola e in opere davanti a Dio e a tutto il popolo –Luca 24:19. Avevano la loro percezione privata di chi fosse il Cristo, ma stavano vedendo …attraverso uno specchio, in modo confuso… –1 Corinzi 13:12. La loro conoscenza parziale si appoggiava pesantemente sulla loro comprensione e cercava il tipo sbagliato di redenzione. Per loro, il loro redentore era (al passato) un profeta che non poteva più fare ciò che volevano che facesse. Tutti vogliamo che Gesù risolva i nostri problemi e ci faccia sentire meglio, ma il Suo scopo è liberarci dalla nostra presunzione e dal peccato.

Giacobbe aveva ogni ragione di credere che il diritto di primogenitura e la benedizione dovessero essere suoi. A Betel, Dio gli aveva promesso di benedirlo. Giacobbe si aspettava che questo si realizzasse in una forma materiale. E Giacobbe fece voto, dicendo: Se Dio sarà con me, e mi custodirà nel cammino ove io vado, e mi darà pane da mangiare e vestito da mettere, e io ritornassi sano alla casa di mio padre, allora il SIGNORE sarà il mio Dio –Genesi 28:20-21.

Ma la più grande benedizione che mai ricevette da Dio gli giunse sulle ali di una notte profonda e oscura. E Giacobbe restò solo; e lottò con lui un uomo fino al levar dell'alba. E quando vide che non prevaleva contro di lui, toccò l'anca di Giacobbe; e l'anca di Giacobbe si saccò, mentre lottava con lui. E disse: Lasciami andare, perché il giorno è sorto. E disse: Non ti lascerò andare, se prima non mi benedici. E dissegli: Qual è il tuo nome? Ed egli rispose: Giacobbe. E dissegli: Non sarai più chiamato Giacobbe, ma Israele; perché come principe hai prevalso con Dio e con gli uomini e hai prevalso –Genesi 32:24-28.

Giacobbe aveva già accumulato un'abbondanza di beni terreni. Che cosa poteva volere di più? Fu una notte oscura per Giacobbe quando scoprì d'aver trascorso la vita inseguendo beni e resistendo a Dio. Ora cerca il carattere divino e l'abbondanza spirituale. La sua vittoria venne attraverso la resa, e si allontanò zoppicando come uno storpio con una corona. Il Signore non può benedire pienamente un uomo finché non ha prima conquistato i suoi poteri di ragione.

…Destino avverso

E come i sommi sacerdoti e i nostri capi l'hanno consegnato per farlo condannare a morte, e l'hanno crocifisso –Luca 24:20. Dio è specialista nel trasformare gravi dilemmi in vittorie monumentali. Eppure, l'uomo guarda intorno a sé e maledice l'oscurità che lo circonda. Sebbene possa esserci una raffica di bene a ricambiare, …la mattina per loro è come l'ombra della morte… –Giobbe 24:17. Mettere un'enfatizzazione eccessiva sul male che ci circonda è deridere la divinità di Dio. Sebbene tutti possiamo rammaricarci a volte di cose che avremmo potuto fare o dire diversamente, dobbiamo invariabilmente lasciare i risultati nelle mani di Dio. Giobbe sperimentò tanto destino avverso quanto chiunque. Tanto che egli aprì …la bocca e maledisse il suo giorno. E Giobbe parlò e disse: Perisca il giorno in cui sono nato, e la notte in cui fu detto: È stato concepito un uomo. Sia quel giorno tenebra; non lo riguardi Dio dall'alto, e non risplenda su esso la luce. Tenebra e l'ombra di morte lo coprano; una nube dimori sopra di esso; ne spaventi l'oscurità. E per quella notte, che la tenebra la prenda… –Giobbe 3:1-6. Ma da qualche parte, prima che gli avvenimenti oscuri venissero rettificati e sollevati, la luce brillò nella sua anima, e pose la mano sulla bocca e adorò.

…Agenda personale

Ma noi speravamo che egli fosse colui che aveva da riscattare Israele… –Luca 24:21. È naturale tentare di capire una data situazione e questi due avevano scelto l'equazione corretta. La loro follia stava nella presunzione dei mezzi con cui Cristo avrebbe compiuto questo e nel tipo di redenzione che si attendevano di ricevere. Attendevano il giorno in cui la loro nazione sarebbe stata esaltata sopra i Romani. Quando inconsapevolmente cerchiamo la nostra sicurezza, siamo destinati a una amara delusione. Naamàn pensava …Egli certo verrà fuori a me, e si metterà in piedi e invocando il nome del SIGNORE suo Dio, batterà con la mano sul luogo e guarirà il lebbroso –2 Re 5:11.

Abramo gli era stata promessa la terra di Canaan e chiese una conferma. Poi preparò il sacrificio del patto prescritto da Dio, ma l'intera giornata passò, e Dio non fece nulla con loro. E quando il sole tramontava, cadde su Abramo un sonno profondo; ed ecco, un terrore di grande oscurità lo avvolse –Genesi 15:12.

Mentre Abramo aspettava che Dio accettasse la sua offerta, continuò a scacciare gli uccelli rapaci. Ma quando il giorno stava per finire cominciò a sentirsi abbandonato da Dio e la notte oscura cominciò a posarsi sulla sua anima. Ci vuole un'esperienza di mezzanotte perché le cose diventino abbastanza buie da poter vedere le stelle e abbastanza silenziose da udire la Sua voce. Ma avemmo dentro noi la sentenza di morte, affinché non confidassimo in noi stessi, ma in Dio che risuscita i morti –2 Corinzi 1:9.

…Impazienza

…E oltre a tutto questo, oggi è il terzo giorno da quando queste cose sono avvenute –Luca 24:21. Molti di noi sono abbastanza disciplinati da resistere per un tempo. È quando la nostra speranza è differita (vedi Proverbi 13:12) che il nostro cuore si ammala e si smarrisce. Tre giorni sembravano un lungo periodo a questi due. Ma tre giorni, settimane, mesi, anni o persino decenni sono tutti nel dominio dell'orologio di Dio. Fino a quando, SIGNORE, mi dimenticherai in eterno? fino a quando nasconderai il tuo volto da me? –Salmo 13:1.

Giuseppe sopportò pazientemente il cattivo trattamento dei suoi fratelli e di Potifar, ma il carcere divenne lungo, e implorò il coppiere di ricordarsi di lui quando fosse stato riabilitato. Ma passarono due anni pieni (Genesi 41:1) prima che il faraone sognasse e Giuseppe fosse finalmente chiamato. Ma non fu tanto colpa del coppiere quanto della volontà di Dio che aveva chiamato Giuseppe a essere …posto in ferro: finché non venne il tempo della sua parola: la parola del SIGNORE lo mise alla prova –Salmo 105:18-19. Non c'è via più efficace per insegnarci la pazienza che la disciplina dell'oscurità, dalla quale pochi santi sono esenti.

…Autocommiserazione

Sì, e alcune donne pure del nostro gruppo vennero al sepolcro molto presto; e quando non trovarono il suo corpo, vennero dicendo che avevano anche visto una visione di angeli, i quali dicevano che egli vive –Luca 24:22-23. A nessuno piace essere escluso. In effetti, la psicologia ha scoperto un nuovo disturbo—FOMO (fear of missing out), la paura di perdersi qualcosa. La notizia portata dalle donne era buona e un sorprendente rovesciamento degli eventi, tuttavia non portò gioia agli altri perché non era capitato a loro. Una buona notizia difficilmente può penetrare in una persona immersa nell'autocommiserazione ed Elia fu uno di questi. La sua notte oscura giunse sulle ali di un trionfo mozzafiato sul monte Carmelo contro i profeti di Baal. Ma nell'oscurità dei suoi sentimenti interni …pregò per sé dicendo: Basta, ora, o SIGNORE, toglimi la vita; perché io non sono meglio dei miei padri –1 Re 19:4.

…Sensazioni di fallimento

Alcuni di quelli che erano con noi andarono al sepolcro e trovarono le cose così come le donne avevan detto; ma lui non l'hanno visto –Luca 24:24. È facile pensare: «Ha funzionato per loro ma non sta funzionando per me». Sebbene sforzi infruttuosi possano scoraggiarci, non è necessariamente un fallimento da parte nostra. Giovanni Battista aveva fedelmente chiamato la gente al pentimento, battezzò Cristo e udì la voce tonante dal cielo. Annunciò accuratamente il Messia che doveva venire e indicò ai suoi discepoli …l'Agnello di Dio che toglie il peccato del mondo –Giovanni 1:29. Questo ministero gli guadagnò un sicuro posto in una cella oscura. Era ben abituato alla mancanza di conforto e a una dieta magra, ma furono i sentimenti di totale abbandono da parte di Dio a condurlo a scuri dubbi. E Giovanni, chiamati due dei suoi discepoli, li mandò a Gesù, dicendo: Sei tu colui che deve venire, o ne aspettiamo un altro? –Luca 7:19.

«Ho sbagliato?» Nell'oscurità cominciò a sperimentare la vita sulla schiena inclinata di un punto interrogativo. John Bunyan lo descrive come il pantano della disperazione. Potrebbe sembrare il D-Day per il cristiano, ma porre troppa enfasi sui nostri sforzi falliti non promuove alcuna risurrezione.

Conclusione

Non tutto l'oscurità spirituale è completamente evitabile. Non ogni esperienza spirituale è un tempo di benedizione sentita, né lo è ogni luogo. Ci sono tempi di persecuzione e di prova che sono pensati per condurre i santi a un rendiconto dell'anima che solo le notti oscure possono svolgere. Lo stesso Gesù fu tentato in modo simile a noi, quando nell'oscuro prevalere della nona ora sulla croce, la Sua voce risuonò …in alta voce, dicendo: Eli, Eli, lama sabactani? che si traduce: Dio mio, Dio mio, perché mi hai abbandonato? –Matteo 27:46.

La via per Emmaus testimonia il fatto che un'esistenza viva di fede non garantisce l'assenza di depressione spirituale. È la storia di persone reali con fede reale che sperimentano prove reali. Ci aiuta a capire che anche i piaceri spirituali non dovrebbero essere tenuti troppo strette. Le nostre visioni fiduciose per il futuro, sia immediato che a lungo termine, devono essere immerse nei fuochi dell'umiltà. La notte oscura è il luogo dove tale autoinganno muore e nasce una conoscenza intima di Dio. Essa ci trasforma dall'amare Dio per le benedizioni che ci dà, all'amare Dio per la nostra relazione con Lui e la comunione che ne deriva.

Il compagno di viaggio di Cleopa non fu mai menzionato. Alcuni pensano fosse sua moglie. Altri affermano fosse Luca. Ma la loro identità fu omessa, forse affinché noi siamo più inclini a riempire il vuoto con il nostro proprio nome. A sette miglia da Gerusalemme inciampiamo nella cruda realtà di chi sia realmente il Salvatore e che la salvezza è più che un semplice timbro di possesso. Le scaglie cadono dai nostri occhi e la notte oscura dell'anima cede il passo allo splendore della luce di mezzogiorno della presenza di Dio. È allora che compiamo la nostra corsa gioiosa verso la città della pace solo per essere nuovamente fraintesi. E andarono e lo riferirono agli altri; ma non credettero loro –Marco 16:13.

E così, mi stupisco persino della convenienza di mettere per iscritto tali pensieri. Non è un incontro che si possa fabbricare e comprendere intellettualmente. È una convocazione altamente personale con Dio e su misura specificamente per ogni individuo. Ma forse noi, nella nostra generazione superficiale, possiamo essere incoraggiati a tendere la mano e abbracciare l'oscurità anziché incontrarla con un rifiuto carico d'odio. E lì, nella minacciosa oscurità della notte, imparare ad abbracciare il Salvatore della luce.

Lunga giaceva prigioniera la mia anima,
Legata stretta al peccato e alla notte della natura.
Il tuo occhio diffuse un raggio vivificante,
Mi destai; la prigione si incendiò di luce.
Le mie catene caddero. Il mio cuore fu libero.
Mi alzai, uscii e ti seguii.

- Charles Wesley
