This is the first of a series of articles on “Discipleship.” Today, Jesus is continuing to call men and women to respond to the simple call, “Follow Me.” Jesus is calling each of us to personally “Follow Me.” In this series, we will explore the depth of this simple command of Jesus. Like the disciples, you will find yourself drawn to follow Jesus.

You may experience both exhilaration and apprehension. Exhilaration, as your journey of faith takes you to heights of love that you have never known. Apprehension, as your faith is tested in new and difficult ways.

There is an emptiness in every human heart that only Jesus can fill. There is a purity and beauty in the life of Jesus that resonates with those heart longings. As we walk with Jesus, we find ourselves being transformed. Old things pass away. All things become new. His life becomes our life. His desires become our desires.

Discipleship is incumbent on the believer. Believing in Jesus, repenting of our sins, and receiving the Lord Jesus into our heart are the first steps into a lifelong journey of faith. Discipleship is not an alternate means of salvation. Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free. Following Jesus is not a carnal attempt to merit eternal life. It is the love response of one who has discovered the source of life.

If you join us on this journey, you will discover that following Jesus will lead us into the valley of decision where we will find ourselves compelled to choose between a life of total surrender to Christ or a life of sin and pleasing self.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagine yourself in a ship with one of these brethren. The sun was rising on the eastern horizon. Anticipating another day of fishing the blue waters of the Galilee, you busy yourself with the daily tasks. Fishing has been your life. You are as much at home on the sea as you are in your cottage.

Another day, another catch of fish, and you should be able to keep the creditors at bay for another week. It’s the only life you have ever known. Your father was a fisherman. Your grandfather was a fisherman. It’s a comfortable life. It’s a familiar life.

This morning, as the waves are gently lapping the sandy shoreline, a man approaches. He’s not a total stranger. Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son. He astounds the local rabbi with his knowledge of the scriptures. His character is flawless; He is the friend of all and a stranger to none.

This man, Jesus (that is his name) is drawing near to your ship. As He draws near, He calls out in a rather cheerful voice, “Follow me.”

James looks at John, and together they look to their father Zebedee. His approving nod was all that they needed. Zebedee had worked with his two sons for many years. Perhaps he was hoping that time with the Nazarene would soften the temper of their abrasive characters.

“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” That’s what He called out to Peter and Andrew. They left their little boat full of nets, perhaps tethered to a stump by the shore. What was it about this Man that He could draw disciples after Him with a simple “Follow Me”? Maybe it was a deep longing in the heart of these disciples—a “hope” that following Jesus might fulfill.

Generations of Jewish men had been looking for The Messiah—The Promised One; He who would break the Roman yoke and restore Israel to her former freedom and glory. Jesus was the most promising revolutionary prospect of the day. He would need a following. He would need their help. Little did they realize that day as they dropped their nets and followed Jesus where that journey would lead them. Little did they know that if they followed this Man, they would never be the same.

As Peter, Andrew, James, and John joined with eight others to follow Jesus, they were walking away from the familiar, secure life of the fisherman. They may have thought that following Jesus would be an adventure. They may have thought that after a term of service to the Nazarene, they could return to their fishing boats. As a matter of fact, that is what they did.

After Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection, He made several appearances to His disciples. They had not yet received the Holy Spirit, and, in the midst of this great uncertainty, they could not resist the allure of the familiar. They decided to go fishing, but much to their consternation they had lost the touch. They fished all night and caught nothing. In the morning Jesus was standing on the shore. He told them to cast on the right side of the ship. They cast and were not able to pull in the nets due to the multitude of fish.

Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No. And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes –John 21:3-6.

Have you ever found yourself in a position where you have tried and tried and all your efforts are met with failure? You know what it is to “reach the end of my hoarded resources”. If that is where you find yourself, you are in a position to experience a miracle. God shows himself strong to those who acknowledge their weakness.

When you decide to follow Jesus, He will draw you into such an utter dependence upon Him that you will finally no longer trust in yourself. To become truly like Jesus is to realize with Paul …that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing…. Paul then continues the verse …for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not –Romans 7:18.

Discipleship will lead us into a total abandonment of ourselves to Christ. Just as the disciples could not have fathomed where following Jesus would lead them, neither can we. We make a faith choice. We choose to follow. We commit the details to our Master.

If you want to be like Jesus, you cannot look back. Jesus said: …No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62. Peter looked back. He said, “I go a fishing”. Disillusioned following the crucifixion and glorious resurrection, Peter chose to return to the lifestyle that was familiar to him. He went back to fishing and James and John went with him.

When Jesus appeared on the shore after their long night of fruitless toil, He prepared a fish fry for the weary disciples. As Peter sat munching on a charbroiled fish, Jesus turned to him and said, “Peter, do you love Me more than these?” How gently piercing are the words of Jesus.

Peter responded, “Yes Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.” We do not know how much time passed, but Jesus turned to him again, “Peter…” (actually He called him Simon) “Do you love Me?” Peter gave the same staid response. “Yes Lord, you know that I love you”. It was the right answer, but Jesus was interested in more than just a right answer, so He said to him again, “Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me?”

Peter finally began to feel that Jesus was asking for something more of him—something that pierced his soul through and through. He had begun following Jesus with the desire to receive from Him. Now Jesus is asking him to reciprocate that love.

Scenes of Caiaphas’ house came before him. He saw Jesus being brutally handled, falsely accused, and spat upon. He heard the angry shouting of the Sanhedrin as they called for Jesus’ death. And then there was that persistent young damsel that challenged him that he was one of Jesus’ disciples. He said to her, “I am not”. Three times he had denied knowing Jesus and now three times Jesus has challenged his love.

In anguish of heart Peter cried out, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee”. Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep”. From that day, Peter was a man with a calling, not only to know Christ for the purpose of receiving from him, but also to emulate him. Discipleship is more than merely knowing about Jesus. Discipleship is walking in his footsteps and identifying with Jesus in his ministry and in his sufferings—truly knowing Him.

Jesus is asking you today, “Do you love me?” We all know the right answer, “Yes, of course, I love Jesus.” Then “Love your neighbor” – “Serve the needy” – “Defer to your brother” – “Forgive the one that has offended you”.

Discipleship is very practical in that it moves us beyond the ideological and causes us to become the very hands and feet of Jesus to those around us.

If in your heart you are thinking, this doesn’t sound very appealing, I would encourage you to focus on the moment and the task at hand. Peter walked with Jesus for three and a half years before he received this call from Jesus. Jesus never calls us without equipping us, and He doesn’t equip us until He determines that we are ready. After the Day of Pentecost, Peter was called, he was prepared, and he was equipped. Then God used him mightily to establish the church.

I would like to call your attention to another attribute of discipleship that is sometimes misplaced. Discipleship is never intended to be drudgery. If you find following Jesus to be hard and toilsome, that is evidence that your love has not yet been perfected.

Jesus’ soul-piercing question to Peter was quite simple, “Do you love Me?” It was as if Jesus was testing Peter. [“I have a job for you, Peter, but a prerequisite for this job is your devoted love for Me.”] Discipleship is a love response to Jesus. Our love for Christ makes service a joy. Toil is pleasant and sacrifice is not a loss.

We can best understand this in the context of human relationships. If you are married and you truly love your husband or your wife, you do not even consider it a sacrifice to work for the mutual benefit of your marriage. In the same way, if we are truly in love with Jesus it is not considered toil to work for him. No sacrifice that we make for the kingdom of heaven is a loss.

I welcome you to join us as we explore the realities of discipleship. We will learn from Christ’s example of forgiveness. We will gain a greater understanding of what it means to walk by faith. Jesus taught us to not worry but to trust. He taught lessons on servant leadership and on cross bearing. There is so much to discover when we are walking with Jesus.

Expect to be changed. The teachings of Jesus are revolutionary in that they run counter to our human impulses. Purpose to allow the life of Christ to become your life and you will be amazed by what God will do for you.

这是关于“门徒训练”的系列文章中的第一篇。今天，耶稣仍在继续呼召男女回应那简单的呼唤：“跟随我。”耶稣在呼召我们每一个人个人地“跟随我”。在本系列中，我们要探讨耶稣这一简单命令的深意。像门徒一样，你会发现自己被吸引去跟随耶稣。

你可能会既感到振奋又感到不安。振奋，因为你的信仰之旅会带你到未曾体会过的爱的高度。不安，因为你的信心将以新的和艰难的方式受到考验。

每个人心中都有一种空虚，只有耶稣能填满。耶稣生平中有一种纯净与美丽，与那些心灵的渴慕产生共鸣。当我们与耶稣同行时，我们发现自己正在被改变。旧事已过，一切都变成了新事。他的生命成为我们的生命。他的愿望成为我们的愿望。

门徒训练是信徒的当务之事。信靠耶稣、为我们的罪悔改并把主耶稣接入我们的心，是踏上终身信仰旅程的第一步。门徒训练并非另一种得救的途径。跟随耶稣是得自由的灵魂的回应。跟随耶稣不是凭肉体去争取永生的努力。这是发现生命源头者的爱之回应。

若你与我们同行，你会发现跟随耶稣会把我们带入抉择的谷底，在那里我们被迫在完全向基督降服的生活与属罪、取悦己的生活之间做出选择。

耶稣在加利利海边行走的时候，看见两个兄弟，就是称为彼得的西门和他兄弟安得烈，在海里撒网，因为他们是打鱼的。他对他们说，跟随我，我要叫你们得人如得鱼一样。他们就立刻舍了网，跟从了他。他从那里往前走，看见另两个兄弟，就是西庇太的儿子雅各和他兄弟约翰，在船上同他们的父亲西庇太修网，他就招呼他们。他们就立刻舍了船和父亲，跟从了他——马太福音 4:18-22。

想象你正与其中一位兄弟同在一条船上。太阳在东方地平线上升起。你期待着又一天在加利利的碧水中捕鱼，忙于日常的事务。打鱼一直是你的生活。你在海上如在自己的小屋中般自在。

又是新的一天，又是一网鱼，你应该能让债主再忍耐一周。这是你所知的唯一生活。你的父亲是渔夫，你的祖父也是渔夫。这是安稳的生活，是熟悉的生活。

今晨，当波浪轻拍着沙岸时，有一个人走近。他并非完全陌生。人人都知道玛利亚的儿子。人人对玛利亚的儿子各有看法。他以对圣经的知识使当地的拉比惊讶。他的品格无可指摘；他是众人的朋友，毫无陌生人。

这个人，名叫耶稣，正向你的船靠近。当他靠近时，他以相当欢快的声音呼唤说：“跟随我。”

雅各看着约翰，他们一同望向父亲西庇太。他的赞许点头就是他们所需要的一切。西庇太与他的两个儿子一起工作了许多年。或许他希望与那拿撒勒人同在的时光会软化他们粗暴性情中的棱角。

“跟随我，我要叫你们得人如得鱼一样。”他就是这样呼召彼得和安得烈。他们舍下满是网的小船，或许把船系在岸边的树桩上。是什么使这位能够以一句简单的“跟随我”就吸引门徒跟随他？也许这是门徒们心中深处的一种渴望——一种“盼望”，跟随耶稣可能会成全这种盼望。

几代犹太人一直在寻找弥赛亚——那位被应许者；那位要打破罗马枷锁并恢复以色列往昔自由与荣耀的那一位。耶稣在当时是最有希望的革命性人物。他需要跟随者。他需要他们的帮助。那天，当他们放下网跟随耶稣时，他们几乎无法预见那条路将把他们带到何处。他们也不知道，若他们跟随这位，他们将不再相同。

当彼得、安得烈、雅各和约翰与另外八人一同跟随耶稣时，他们正走离渔夫那熟悉而安全的生活。他们或许以为跟随耶稣会是一场冒险。他们或许以为服事拿撒勒人一段时间后，可以回到他们的渔船。事实上，他们确实这样做了。

在耶稣被钉十字架和复活之后，他多次向门徒显现。他们尚未领受圣灵，在这极大的不确定中，他们无法抗拒熟悉事物的诱惑。他们决定去打鱼，但令人沮丧的是他们已失去技巧。他们整夜捕鱼一无所获。清晨耶稣站在岸上，告诉他们要向船的右边下网。他们下网，因鱼多，竟拉不动网。

西门彼得对他们说，我要下海打鱼。他们说，我们也和你同去。他们就出去，上了船，立时那夜什么也没有得。到天亮，耶稣站在岸上；门徒却不知道是耶稣。耶稣就对他们说，孩子们，你们有吃的没有？他们回答说，没有。耶稣说，把网撒在船的右边，就必得着。他们于是撒下去，竟拉不起来，因为鱼多得不可胜——约翰福音 21:3-6。

你是否曾处在一种你尽力而为却屡遭失败的境地？你知道什么叫“用尽我积蓄的资源”。如果你正处在那样的境地，你就有可能经历一个神迹。上帝向承认自己软弱的人显明他的能力。

当你决定跟随耶稣时，他会把你引入对他的彻底依靠，以致你终不再信靠自己。要真正成为像耶稣的人，就像保罗所意识到的那样……在我（就是在我肉体里）没有良善可居……保罗随后继续这节经文……因为立志为善在我，我却得不出来行那美善——罗马书 7:18。

门徒训练会把我们带入对基督的完全舍己。正如门徒无法预料跟随耶稣会把他们带到何处，我们也无法。我们做出信心的选择。我们选择跟随。我们将细节交托给我们的师傅。

若你想像耶稣，你不能回头。耶稣说：……手扶着犁向后看的，不配进神的国——路加福音 9:62。彼得回头了。他说，“我要下海打鱼”。在十字架受难和荣耀复活之后失望之中，彼得选择回到他熟悉的生活方式。他回去打鱼，雅各和约翰也与他同去。

当耶稣在他们那一夜无果的劳碌之后出现在岸上，他为疲惫的门徒预备了一顿烤鱼。当彼得坐着啃着烤鱼时，耶稣转向他说，“彼得，你比这些还爱我么？”耶稣的话多么温柔而刺透人心。

彼得回答：“主啊，你知道我爱你。”耶稣说，“喂养我的羊。”我们不知道过了多久，耶稣又转向他，“彼得……”（其实他叫他西门）“你爱我么？”彼得给出同样稳重的回答，“主啊，你知道我爱你。”这是正确的答案，但耶稣要的不仅仅是一个正确的回答，于是他又对他说：“西门（约拿的儿子），你爱我么？”

彼得终于开始感到耶稣向他索要更多的东西——某种透彻刺入他灵魂的东西。他起初是带着从耶稣那里得到的愿望跟随耶稣。如今耶稣要求他回报这种爱。

该亚法家的情景涌现在他眼前。他看见耶稣被粗暴对待，遭受虚假的指控，并被人唾弃。他听见公会愤怒的喊声，呼求耶稣判死。然后有那个固执的小女仆质问他，说他是耶稣的一个门徒。他对她说，“我不是”。他三次否认认识耶稣，而现在耶稣也三次挑战他的爱。

彼得在心灵的痛苦中呼叫：“主啊，你知道万事，你知道我爱你。”耶稣对他说，“牧养我的羊。”从那天起，彼得成了一个被呼召的人，不仅是为着认识基督以便从他那里得着什么，而且也要效法他。门徒训练远不止是对耶稣的知识。门徒训练是行在他的脚踪中，在他的事工和他的受苦中与耶稣认同——真正地认识他。

耶稣今天正在问你，“你爱我么？”我们都知道正确的答案，“是的，当然，我爱耶稣。”接着是“爱你的邻舍”——“服事有需要的人”——“顺服弟兄”——“饶恕冒犯你的人”。

门徒训练非常实用，它使我们超越意识形态，使我们成为耶稣向周围人的手与脚。

若你心里在想，这听起来并不吸引人，我会鼓励你专注于当下与手头的任务。彼得与耶稣同行了三年半，才领受耶稣从他那里的这个呼召。耶稣从不在未装备我们之前呼召我们，他也不会在他确定我们已经准备好之前装备我们。五旬节之后，彼得被呼召、被预备并被装备。随后上帝大大使用他建立教会。

我愿提醒你门徒训练的另一个有时被误置的属性。门徒训练绝非旨在成为苦差事。如果你发现跟随耶稣艰难且劳累，那就是你对他的爱尚未得以完全的证据。

耶稣那穿透心灵的问题对彼得来说相当简单，“你爱我吗？”仿佛耶稣在试验彼得。[“彼得，我有一件事要你做，但这工作的先决条件是你对我的殷勤之爱。”]门徒训练是对耶稣的爱之回应。我们对基督的爱使服事成为喜乐。劳苦变得甘甜，牺牲不再是损失。

我们可以在人人关系的语境中最好地理解这一点。若你已婚并且真心爱你的丈夫或妻子，你为婚姻的互惠利益而工作时，甚至不会把它看作牺牲。同样地，若我们真爱耶稣，为他劳苦并不被视为劳累。为天国所作的任何牺牲都不是损失。

我欢迎你与我们一同探讨门徒训练的现实。我们将从基督的饶恕榜样中学习。我们将更深入地明白何为凭信心行走。耶稣教我们不要忧虑而要信靠。他教导有关仆人式领导和背十字架的功课。当我们与耶稣同行时，有太多可发现的事。

预备被改变。耶稣的教导是革命性的，因为它们与我们人的冲动相违背。立志让基督的生命成为你的生命，你将惊异上帝为你所成就的事。

Around the world, but particularly in the United States, people seem to value rugged individualism. People who demonstrate this character quality make their own way through life, asking nothing from others and expecting nothing.

I suppose that this idea relates back to the pioneers. These were men and women who trekked across the various new countries looking for a place where they could settle down and call home. There were few general stores and as much as possible they lived as self-sufficiently as they could.

While this may sound like a scenario that demonstrates strength, the truth is somewhat different these days. These days people use technology to deliberately create bubbles of isolation around themselves.

Many older people have found themselves increasingly isolated from friends and family. COVID certainly made this worse, but there were seeds of this seclusion that had been sowed long before COVID was ever heard of.

Isolation is Not a Natural State

Looking back to the Garden of Eden we can see that Adam was created before Eve. While there were lots of animals around, there was no true companionship for Adam. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him … And Adam gave names to all cattle, and to the fowl of the air, and to every beast of the field; but for Adam there was not found an help meet for him –Genesis 2:18-20.

And the LORD God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof; And the rib, which the LORD God had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man –Genesis 2:21-22. Of course, this was the beginning of marriage, but the more important thing to see here is that it is not a normal state for humans to be alone. We desire companionship and not just the companionship of a pet dog or cat.

Isolation can lead to Despair

Perhaps there is no story that demonstrates so clearly the dangers of isolation as the story of Elijah. We know from the biblical book of I Kings, that Elijah was a fiery prophet of God.

He brought word from God to Ahab that there would be no rain and there was terrible drought for the next three and a half years. During that time, Elijah spent time in the wilderness and then with a widow in Zarephath.

The whole time, he was miraculously fed through God’s power, first by ravens and then through God’s provision of flour and oil to a widow, with whom he lived. Through God’s power, he raised the widow’s son to life.

Then came a time when he challenged the prophets of Baal to a match on Mt. Carmel and won a decisive victory for God. Miraculous fire descended from heaven in answer to his prayer. Truly, God was working great things in his life.

Very soon though, Elijah was running for his life into the desert. Jezebel had threatened his life and rather than trusting God, he fled to Mt. Horeb where he heard the voice of God.

When God asked him what he was doing there, Elijah replied, …I have been very jealous for the LORD God of hosts: for the children of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thine altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away –1 Kings 19:10.

We can see here a big reason for Elijah’s weakness. He felt completely alone. God corrected Elijah’s incorrect assumption when He stated: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him –1 Kings 19:18.

The fact that those men and women existed in Israel did Elijah little good since he didn’t spend time with them. Elijah’s isolation led him to weakness and despair.

The story of Paul comes to mind as well. The Apostle Paul was a man who seemed to have nearly limitless amounts of energy and an unquenchable zeal for the things of God, but his last letter to Timothy from prison revealed a man who felt very alone. Do thy diligence to come shortly unto me: For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world, and is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark, and bring him with thee… –2 Timothy 4:9-11.

The Apostle was not abandoned. Other than Demas, they had not fled because they were afraid or ashamed of his bonds. He had sent many of his friends away to strengthen the church in various parts of the Roman Empire. Yet, Paul was still feeling isolated and needed the good Christian brothers, Timothy and Mark, to come and encourage him as he faced a martyr’s death.

Isolation is Physically Harmful

Studies have showed that isolation is linked to higher rates of high blood pressure, heart disease, anxiety, and depression. Older people who are isolated often show signs of mental decline and can experience worsening dementia.

Many times, as people age, they experience the deaths of loved ones. The loss of a spouse can lead older people to withdraw from others and to experience loneliness and isolation. This in turn often leads to rapid progression of the aging process.

Science does not fully understand it, but loneliness leads to increased inflammation and poorer immune function. This in turn can lead to lonely people getting worse infections and struggling to recover after such an infection.

While we think of these problems as those that primarily affect elderly people, they can affect younger people as well. In younger people, often loneliness doesn’t lead to memory issues, but it certainly can lead to things like depression, and it can make chronic inflammatory diseases much worse.

The Opposite of Isolation

If asked what the opposite of isolation is most people would probably answer “Companionship” or maybe even “Friendship”. There is another word which has a Christian connotation that is even better. That word is fellowship.

The Greek word translated fellowship in the New Testament is “Koinonia” and in the Bible it speaks of relationships that are founded on a shared love for God and for the church—a unity of belief and desire. Christian fellowship includes concepts like praying together, encouraging one another, and even suffering together.

I am afraid that many today find themselves in one of two dangerous situations. First, they may not be a member of any church congregation. While this may be unavoidable in certain mission outreach situations, it is not ideal, and most certainly it should not be a normal situation. At the very least it can create a sense of isolation, and at the worst it hinders many of the “one-anothering” Bible passages from being followed. We need fellowship, both to encourage us and to keep us accountable.

The second dangerous situation is that many believers, while members of a church, isolate themselves within that church. If you are a member of a large church congregation, it is easy to blend in and not develop relationships with others. This is just as harmful as not being a member of a church body. Too many people feel lonely, even when there are lots of people around.

Scripture makes it clear that we need a church body. Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching –Hebrews 10:25.

There are many people who have lives that are full of friends and acquaintances, but if they do not have a place where they receive fellowship, they are missing out.

When I see people in my office who are struggling with depression there are two things I always tell them to do for themselves.

First is to start exercising. There have been several studies that compared exercise to antidepressants and found that it had similar effectiveness to many of the commonly prescribed antidepressant medications. This doesn’t have to be really vigorous exercise, but it does need to be aerobic (enough to raise the heart rate) and consistent.

The second is to become active in a church congregation; it is not enough to just attend church. Having brothers and sisters to pray for someone who is struggling, to listen to the discouraging situations, and to encourage that person to a more vibrant walk with God is really helpful.

Unfortunately, when someone is struggling with depression, the last thing they seem to want to do is make the effort to be around other people, which contrary to their feelings, is counterproductive to changing the problem.

As we consider this, it should move us to reach out to those who we know are struggling with isolation.

When someone loses a spouse, they often have a lot of encouragement for the first several weeks, but we need to make certain that they continue to have an active presence in their lives in the months that follow.

For every man shall bear his own burden –Galatians 6:5, should not give us excuse to not obey God’s command to Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2. The family of God is given no time limit on bearing burdens. There is only a mandate that as we see our brother or sister struggling, we are to help them, as we are able.

The blessing is that someday, when we are struggling, we will have men and women of faith around us to encourage us and to pray for us. We cannot carry these burdens alone. Together, we will reach the Celestial City.

Isolation comes for many reasons. Sometimes it seems to be a chosen way of life, as is the natural tendency of introverted people. Sometimes it is foisted upon a person due to deaths of loved ones or other significant losses. Either way, it is not a healthy place to live.

As we find ourselves in these situations, we need to reach out for fellowship. The family of God is there for us if we only reach out.

As we see others who are struggling, we need to extend to them the right arm of fellowship. As we do so, we may, through our small efforts, help someone emotionally, physically, and spiritually, simply by being a friend in a time of isolation.

Di seluruh dunia, tetapi terutama di Amerika Serikat, tampaknya orang menghargai individualisme yang tangguh. Orang-orang yang menunjukkan ciri karakter ini menapaki hidup mereka sendiri, tidak meminta apa pun dari orang lain dan tidak mengharapkan apa pun.

Saya kira gagasan ini berakar pada para perintis. Mereka adalah pria dan wanita yang menempuh perjalanan melintasi berbagai negeri baru mencari tempat di mana mereka bisa menetap dan menyebutnya rumah. Hanya ada sedikit toko umum dan sebisa mungkin mereka hidup semandiri mungkin.

Meskipun ini mungkin terdengar seperti skenario yang menunjukkan kekuatan, kenyataannya agak berbeda sekarang. Saat ini orang menggunakan teknologi untuk sengaja menciptakan gelembung isolasi di sekitar diri mereka.

Banyak orang lanjut usia mendapati diri mereka semakin terasing dari teman dan keluarga. COVID tentu membuat ini lebih buruk, tetapi benih pengasingan ini telah ditabur jauh sebelum COVID pernah terdengar.

Isolasi Bukanlah Keadaan Alamiah

Melihat kembali ke Taman Eden kita dapat melihat bahwa Adam diciptakan sebelum Hawa. Walaupun ada banyak binatang di sekitar, tidak ada teman sejati bagi Adam. Dan TUHAN Allah berfirman: Tidak baik, kalau manusia itu seorang diri saja; Aku akan menjadikan penolong baginya, yang sepadan dengan dia … Dan Adam memberi nama kepada segala ternak, dan kepada burung-burung di udara, dan kepada segala binatang di padang; tetapi bagi Adam tidak didapati penolong yang sepadan dengan dia – Kejadian 2:18-20.

Lalu TUHAN Allah membuat manusia itu jatuh ke dalam tidur nyenyak, dan ketika ia tidur, Ia mengambil salah satu rusuknya dan menutup tempat itu dengan daging. Maka dari rusuk yang diambil TUHAN Allah dari manusia itu dijadikan-Nya seorang perempuan dan dibawa kepada manusia itu – Kejadian 2:21-22. Tentu saja, ini adalah permulaan perkawinan, tetapi hal yang lebih penting untuk dilihat di sini adalah bahwa bukanlah keadaan normal bagi manusia untuk sendirian. Kita menginginkan persekutuan, bukan sekadar kebersamaan dengan anjing atau kucing peliharaan.

Isolasi Dapat Menyebabkan Keputusasaan

Mungkin tidak ada cerita yang menunjukkan dengan begitu jelas bahaya isolasi seperti kisah Elia. Kita tahu dari kitab 1 Raja-raja bahwa Elia adalah nabi yang bersemangat bagi Allah.

Ia menyampaikan firman dari Allah kepada Ahab bahwa tidak akan turun hujan dan terjadi kekeringan yang parah selama tiga setengah tahun berikutnya. Selama waktu itu, Elia menghabiskan waktu di padang gurun dan kemudian bersama seorang janda di Sarefat.

Sepanjang waktu itu, ia diberi makan secara mujizat oleh kuasa Allah, pertama oleh burung gagak dan kemudian oleh penyediaan tepung dan minyak yang diberikan Allah kepada seorang janda tempat ia tinggal. Melalui kuasa Allah, ia membangkitkan anak janda itu dari kematian.

Lalu datanglah waktu ketika ia menantang nabi-nabi Baal untuk bertanding di Gunung Karmel dan memenangkan kemenangan yang menentukan bagi Allah. Api mukjizat turun dari langit sebagai jawaban atas doanya. Benar-benar, Allah sedang melakukan pekerjaan besar dalam hidupnya.

Namun tak lama kemudian, Elia melarikan diri untuk menyelamatkan nyawanya ke padang gurun. Izebel telah mengancam nyawanya dan bukannya mempercayai Allah, ia lari ke gunung Horeb tempat ia mendengar suara Allah.

Ketika Allah bertanya kepadanya apa yang dilakukannya di sana, Elia menjawab, …aku sangat cemburu karena TUHAN semesta alam; sebab orang Israel telah meninggalkan perjanjian-Mu, meruntuhkan mezbah- Mezbah-Mu dan membunuh nabi-nabi-Mu dengan pedang; dan aku sendiri ini seorang saja yang tinggal, sedang mereka mencari nyawaku untuk mengambilnya – 1 Raja-raja 19:10.

Kita dapat melihat di sini alasan besar kelemahan Elia. Ia merasa benar-benar sendirian. Allah memperbaiki anggapan salah Elia ketika Dia menyatakan: Namun Aku meninggalkan bagi-Ku tujuh ribu orang di Israel, semua yang lututnya belum sujud kepada Baal, dan setiap mulut yang belum menciumnya – 1 Raja-raja 19:18.

Keniscayaan bahwa orang-orang itu ada di Israel tidak banyak membantu Elia karena ia tidak menghabiskan waktu bersama mereka. Isolasi Elia membawanya kepada kelemahan dan keputusasaan.

Kisah Paulus juga terlintas dalam pikiran. Rasul Paulus adalah orang yang tampaknya memiliki energi nyaris tak terbatas dan semangat yang tak pernah padam untuk hal-hal Allah, tetapi surat terakhirnya kepada Timotius dari penjara memperlihatkan seorang yang merasa sangat sendiri. Bergegaslah datang kepadaku secepatnya: Sebab Demas telah meninggalkanku, karena ia lebih menyukai zaman ini dan telah pergi ke Tesalonika; Kresens ke Galatia, Titus ke Dalmatia. Hanya Lukas yang menyertai aku. Ambillah Markus dan bawalah dia denganmu… – 2 Timotius 4:9-11.

Rasul itu tidak ditinggalkan. Selain Demas, mereka tidak lari karena takut atau malu akan belenggunya. Ia telah mengirim banyak sahabatnya untuk memperkuat jemaat di berbagai bagian Kekaisaran Romawi. Namun, Paulus masih merasakan keterasingan dan membutuhkan saudara-saudara Kristen yang baik, Timotius dan Markus, datang meneguhkan dia ketika ia menghadapi kematian sebagai martir.

Isolasi Berbahaya Secara Fisik

Studi menunjukkan bahwa isolasi terkait dengan tingkat tekanan darah tinggi, penyakit jantung, kecemasan, dan depresi yang lebih tinggi. Orang lanjut usia yang terisolasi sering menunjukkan tanda-tanda penurunan mental dan dapat mengalami memburuknya demensia.

Sering kali, seiring bertambahnya usia, orang mengalami kematian orang-orang yang mereka kasihi. Kehilangan pasangan dapat menyebabkan orang lanjut usia menarik diri dari orang lain dan mengalami kesepian serta pengasingan. Ini pada gilirannya sering mempercepat proses penuaan.

Ilmu pengetahuan belum sepenuhnya memahaminya, tetapi kesepian meningkatkan peradangan dan menurunkan fungsi kekebalan tubuh. Ini pada gilirannya bisa membuat orang yang kesepian mengalami infeksi yang lebih parah dan kesulitan pulih setelah infeksi semacam itu.

Sementara kita menganggap masalah ini terutama memengaruhi orang tua, mereka juga dapat memengaruhi orang yang lebih muda. Pada orang muda, sering kali kesepian tidak menyebabkan masalah memori, tetapi itu tentu dapat menyebabkan hal-hal seperti depresi, dan dapat memperburuk penyakit inflamasi kronis.

Lawan dari Isolasi

Jika ditanya apa lawan dari isolasi kebanyakan orang mungkin akan menjawab “Kebersamaan” atau bahkan “Persahabatan”. Ada satu kata lain yang memiliki konotasi Kristen yang bahkan lebih tepat. Kata itu adalah persekutuan.

Kata Yunani yang diterjemahkan sebagai persekutuan dalam Perjanjian Baru adalah “Koinonia” dan dalam Alkitab itu berbicara tentang hubungan yang didasarkan pada kasih yang sama terhadap Allah dan terhadap jemaat—sebuah kesatuan iman dan hasrat. Persekutuan Kristen mencakup konsep seperti berdoa bersama, saling menguatkan, dan bahkan menderita bersama.

Saya takut banyak orang saat ini mendapati diri mereka dalam salah satu dari dua situasi yang berbahaya. Pertama, mereka mungkin bukan anggota suatu jemaat gereja manapun. Meskipun ini mungkin tidak terelakkan dalam situasi penginjilan tertentu, itu tidak ideal, dan tentu saja tidak seharusnya menjadi keadaan biasa. Paling tidak hal itu dapat menciptakan rasa terasing, dan paling buruk hal itu menghalangi banyak ayat Alkitab tentang saling melayani untuk diikuti. Kita membutuhkan persekutuan, baik untuk menguatkan kita maupun untuk membuat kita bertanggung jawab.

Situasi berbahaya kedua adalah banyak orang percaya, meskipun menjadi anggota gereja, mengisolasi diri di dalam gereja itu sendiri. Jika Anda anggota jemaat yang besar, mudah untuk bercampur dan tidak mengembangkan hubungan dengan orang lain. Ini sama bahayanya dengan tidak menjadi anggota tubuh gereja. Terlalu banyak orang merasa kesepian, bahkan ketika ada banyak orang di sekitar.

Skriptur jelas menunjukkan bahwa kita membutuhkan tubuh gereja. Janganlah kita menjauhkan diri dari pertemuan-pertemuan ibadah kita, seperti yang menjadi kebiasaan beberapa orang, tetapi marilah kita saling menasihati, dan semakin giat melakukannya menjelang hari yang mendekat – Ibrani 10:25.

Ada banyak orang yang kehidupannya penuh dengan teman dan kenalan, tetapi jika mereka tidak memiliki tempat di mana mereka menerima persekutuan, mereka kehilangan sesuatu yang penting.

Ketika saya melihat orang di kantor saya yang bergumul dengan depresi ada dua hal yang selalu saya sarankan agar mereka lakukan untuk diri mereka sendiri.

Yang pertama adalah mulai berolahraga. Ada beberapa studi yang membandingkan olahraga dengan antidepresan dan menemukan bahwa efektivitasnya mirip dengan banyak obat antidepresan yang umum diresepkan. Ini tidak harus olahraga yang sangat berat, tetapi harus bersifat aerobik (cukup untuk meningkatkan detak jantung) dan konsisten.

Yang kedua adalah menjadi aktif di dalam suatu jemaat gereja; tidak cukup hanya menghadiri kebaktian. Memiliki saudara dan saudari yang mendoakan seseorang yang sedang bergumul, mendengarkan situasi yang membuat putus asa, dan mendorong orang itu kepada kehidupan yang lebih bersemangat dalam Tuhan sangatlah membantu.

Saat kita mempertimbangkan hal ini, itu seharusnya mendorong kita untuk meraih mereka yang kita tahu sedang bergumul dengan isolasi.

Ketika seseorang kehilangan pasangan, mereka sering menerima banyak dorongan pada beberapa minggu pertama, tetapi kita harus memastikan bahwa mereka terus memiliki kehadiran aktif dalam hidup mereka pada bulan-bulan berikutnya.

Setiap orang harus memikul tanggungannya sendiri – Galatia 6:5, tidak seharusnya memberi kita alasan untuk tidak taat pada perintah Allah untuk Galatia 6:2: Pikullah bebanmu seorang terhadap yang lain, dan dengan demikian kamu memenuhi hukum Kristus. Keluarga Allah tidak diberikan batas waktu dalam memikul beban. Hanya ada mandat bahwa ketika kita melihat saudara atau saudari kita berjuang, kita harus membantu mereka, sejauh yang kita mampu.

Berkatnya adalah bahwa suatu hari nanti, ketika kita sedang bergumul, kita akan memiliki pria dan wanita beriman di sekitar kita untuk menguatkan dan mendoakan kita. Kita tidak dapat memikul beban ini sendirian. Bersama-sama, kita akan sampai ke Kota Sorga.

Isolasi datang karena banyak alasan. Kadang tampaknya merupakan cara hidup yang dipilih, sebagaimana kecenderungan alami orang introvert. Kadang dipaksakan kepada seseorang karena kematian orang-orang tercinta atau kehilangan signifikan lainnya. Bagaimanapun juga, itu bukan tempat yang sehat untuk tinggal.

Saat kita mendapati diri kita dalam situasi seperti ini, kita perlu meraih persekutuan. Keluarga Allah ada untuk kita jika kita hanya meraih tangan mereka.

Saat kita melihat orang lain yang sedang bergumul, kita perlu mengulurkan tangan persekutuan kepada mereka. Dengan melakukan itu, melalui upaya kecil kita, kita mungkin membantu seseorang secara emosional, fisik, dan rohani, sekadar dengan menjadi seorang teman di masa isolasi.

And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

Na akawaambia, Ni mazungumzo ya aina gani haya ninyi mnayo kwa mwenzenu, mnavyotembea, na mmelemewa? –Luka 24:17.

Mnamo Juni 6, 1944, wanajeshi 156,000 wa Marekani, Uingereza, na Kanada walishuka kwenye ukanda wa ufukwe wa maili 50 huko Normandy, Ufaransa. Baada ya miezi kadhaa ya mapigano makali, waliweza kukabiliana na ulinzi wa awali na kuwafuka walionao Wajerumani. Shambulio la mshangao, lililojulikana kama D-Day, lilimkamata Mungu kishtuko Wajerumani. Hata hivyo, hakukuwa mpaka Machi ya mwaka uliofuata kwamba Ufaransa iliondolewa kabisa kutoka kwa majeshi ya Kijerumani. D-Day ilikuwa mwanzo wa mwisho wa Vita Kuu ya Pili barani Ulaya upande wa magharibi na ilikuwa tukio lililoonekana kumwachilia uhai kutoka kwa jeshi maarufu la Kijerumani, ambalo hawakuwahi kujiponya kutoka kwake. Inaonekana kwa bahati kwamba maneno mengi yenye maana hasi huanza na herufi D: Kukata tamaa, Mashaka, Majuto, Hatima mbaya, Kukata tamaa kwa dhana, Kuchelewesha moyo, Kuzimia, Kushindwa, Kuhuzunika, Mfadhaiko, Kukata tamaa kabisa, Uharibifu, Udanganyifu, na Kifo.

Ninaweza kufikiria kwamba waumini hawa wawili, wakitembea polepole katika barabara ya Emau na kuanguka jioni ile ya giza na huzuni, walihisi kitu kama hicho. D-Day yao ilifika bila kutegemewa kabisa. Ningeshuku kwamba kila mtu hai amewahi wakati fulani kupata nyakati za huzuni kuu—D-day yao, kwa kusema hivyo. Hata baadhi ya wanyama wanajulikana kuonyesha huzuni kwa kifo cha bwana wao au mwenzi. Lakini wanafunzi hawa wawili walionekana kuishi maumivu yaliyo mbali zaidi kuliko kupoteza rafiki wa kawaida. Walikuwa wakitazama uso wa ukweli mbaya kwamba matumaini yao yote yenye kung'aa ya kesho yalivunjika kabisa na kuanguka kabisa katika hula ya uharibifu mzungoni mwa msalaba.

Huu uchungu haukuwa mshtuko wa kawaida wa kukosa hamu bali ulikuwa mfadhaiko uliounganishwa na mgogoro wa imani. Aina hii ya kukata tamaa ni hali ya mateso makali ya kiroho ambapo mwamini anayekabiliana na mashaka anahisi ameachwa na Mungu. Ni hisia ya kukata tamaa kwamba jua la baraka za Mungu limefunikwa na usiku mweusi wa nafsi umekuwa mkazi wa kudumu ndani yake.

Wakati sisi sote tunajitahidi kwa ujasiri kupinga majaribu hayo meusi, utafutaji mfupi katika maisha ya wanaume wengi wanyenyekevu utaonyesha kwamba majaribu haya ni halisi sana na ni ya kawaida kwa mwanadamu. Katika hali kama hiyo, maisha yanaonekana kuwa hayatekelezeki na giza linalokuja juu ya moyo halioni mwanga mwishoni mwa mtundu. Kwani maumivu yangu ya kudumu ni nini, na jeraha langu halipuziwi; haliitai kuponwa? Utakuwa kwangu ujanja, na kama maji yaliyokwisha? –Yeremia 15:18. Hii ni dhihirisho lililozidi kupita kiasi ambalo lilimfukiza mdomo nabii aliyelia, lakini linatupa picha ya moja kwa moja ya maumivu yaliyokuwa ndani ya nafsi yake.

Kwani hatutaki, ndugu, mpate ujinga juu ya taabu yetu iliyotutokea Asia, kwamba tulikandamizwa kupita kiasi, zaidi ya nguvu, hata tukakata tamaa hata ya maisha: Lakini tulikuwa na hukumu ya kifo ndani yetu, ili tusitegemee nafsi zetu, bali Mungu ambaye huteuwa wafu –2 Wakorintho 1:8-9. Usiku mweusi wa nafsi haujali hadhi ya watu. Hunaingilia maisha ya wakuu au maskini, wachungaji au watafakari, watu wa umma na wa kibinafsi, madaraja na viti vya kanisa. Wanafunzi hawa wawili walikagua mdomoni kila tukio linalowezekana walilopita katika safari yao barabarani Emau. Bila shaka walikuwa wamepata makosa mengi kwa wengine pamoja na majuto binafsi. “Je!” na “Kama tu!” vilijadiliwa kwa kina, lakini hakuna kitu kilichoweza kubadilisha matokeo na wasiwasi wao usiotulia ulikuwa bado umetulia.

Barabara kutoka Yerusalemu hadi Emau ilikuwa takriban maili saba au kuhusu threescore furlongs. Na katika safari hii ya huzuni Mgeni alijiunga na wawili waliokuwa na huzuni katika D-Day yao na kuwauliza kuhusu huzuni yao. Lakini yeye si mtazamo mwenye udadisi. Yeye ndiye Bwana aliyefufuka ambaye amekuja kuweka nuru yake ya mbinguni juu ya njia yetu iliyofunikwa giza. Badala ya kujiweka wazi ghafla, na labda kwa ajili yetu, kwa subira anawaacha waonyeshe barabara iliyokauka ya kiroho waliokuwa wakitembea.

Hivyo, mazungumzo yanachanua huku alama za maili zikipita, kila moja ikifunua jitihada zetu batili za kweli ambazo zilituletea mbali na mji wa amani na ndani ya usiku mweusi wa nafsi…

…Kutokujua kwa Wengine

Na mmoja wao, aliyeitwa Kileopa, akajibu akamwambia, Je, wewe pekee ndiye mgeni mjini Yerusalemu, kwamba hukujua mambo yaliyokuwa yametokea huko siku hizi? –Luka 24:18. Muulize mgeni yeyote mitaani mwa Jiji la New York kwanini bendera zilikuwa zimesimama nusu mtawalia siku tatu baada ya minara kuanguka tarehe 11 Septemba, na utapokea jibu la kushangaza lile lile lililotolewa kwa hawa wawili. “Unawezaje kuwa mjinga hivyo?” Sote tunavutiwa watu ambao hawana maarifa yale tunayodhani sisi wenyewe tunayo. Mtu mchanga, ndivyo anavyojiona mwenye majibu mengi anayodhani khazana ya uelewa wake ina vitu vingi.

Hii si jambo jipya. Musa, akiwa kijana, …alikuwa na wazo kwamba ndugu zake wangekuwa wameelewa jinsi gani Mungu kwa mkono wake angewaokoa: lakini hawakuelewa –Matendo 7:25. Ingawa alielewa kwa uimara kwamba alikuwa na mpango wa Mungu, alikosea sana kwa kiasi alichodhani alichomiliki. Ikiwa suluhisho letu haliwezi kurekebisha hali iliyopo, majibu yetu si jibu halisi. Mwonekano wa moyoni unaojitokeza kwa wale wanaoona tofauti ni alama ya mwanzo kwamba tuko kwenye njia mwrong. Maili mbali kwenye njia ya maisha, Musa alianza kuhisi kukata tamaa kwa maumivu hayo na giza la saa. Sina nguvu ya kuvumilia watu wote hawa pekee, kwa maana ni mzito mno kwa ajili yangu. Na ikiwa vitakavyokuwa hivyo kwangu, uniue, tafadhali, mara moja, ikiwa nimepata neema machoni pako; nami nisiondoke kwa kuona umasikini wangu –Hesabu 11:14-15. Kwa nini Musa hakukuona hili mapema maishani? Kwa sababu ile ile kwamba macho yao yalikuwa …yamefungwa wasijue yeye –Luka 24:16.

…Sababu

Na akawaambia, Vitu gani? Wakasema kwake, Kuhusu Yesu wa Nazareti, ambaye alikuwa nabii mwenye nguvu katika matendo na maneno mbele za Mungu na watu wote –Luka 24:19. Walikuwa na mtazamo wao wa binafsi wa nani Kristo alikuwa, lakini walikuwa wanaona …kwa kioo, kwa upuzi… –1 Wakorintho 13:12. Maarifa yao ya sehemu yalitegemea kwa uzito uelewa wao wenyewe na kuhitaji aina isifae ya ukombozi. Kwao, mwokozi wao alikuwa (kwa wakati uliopita) nabii ambaye hakuweza tena kufanya walichomtaka afanye. Sote tunataka Yesu atuwekee suluhisho la matatizo yetu na kutufanya tujihisi vizuri, lakini kusudi Lake ni kutufungua kutoka kwa kudhani na dhambi zetu.

sababu zote za kuamini kwamba haki ya kuzaliwa na baraka zilikuwa zake. Katika Beteli, Mungu alimwahidi kumbariki. Yakobo alifikiria hizi zitakuja kwa njia ya mali. Yakobo akatoa nanga akisema, Ikiwa Mungu atakuwa pamoja nami, na kunihifadhi katika njia hii niliyoongea, na akanipatia mkate niliye kula, na mavazi ya nitoe, Nami nikirudi kwa nyumba ya baba yangu kwa amani; basi BWANA atakuwa Mungu wangu – Mwanzo 28:20-21.

Lakini baraka kubwa kabisa aliyopokea kutoka kwa Mungu ilimtokea katika usiku wa giza kabisa. Yakobo alibaki peke yake; na mtu akampigania hadi kuanguka kwa mchana. Ndipo alipoona kwamba hakuweza kumshinda, akagusa mwili wake eneo la paja; na mwili wa paja la Yakobo ukakatika, alipokuwa akimpigania. Na akamwambia, Niniondoke, kwa maana mchana unaanza. Na akamwambia, Sitakuachilia, ila unibariki. Akamwambia, Je, jina lako nani? Akamwambia, Yakobo. Akamwambia, Sitaambiwi tena jina lako Yakobo, bali Israeli: kwa maana umekuwa mfalme na una mamlaka na Mungu na kwa watu, na umeshinda – Mwanzo 32:24-28.

Yakobo tayari alikuwa amekusanya wingi wa mali za dunia. Alitakiwa kutaka nini zaidi? Ilinakuwa usiku wa giza kwa Yakobo alipogundua kwamba amehangaika maisha yake akitafuta mali na kupinga Mungu. Sasa anatafuta tabia ya kiungu na wingi wa kiroho. Ushindi wake ulikuwa kupitia kukubali, na alienda akiwa na ulemavu akiwa amevaa taji. Bwana hawezi kumbariki mwanadamu kikamilifu hadi kwanza ameshinda nguvu zake za logic.

…Hatima Mbaya

Na jinsi makuhani wakuu na wakuu wetu walimwachiwa ili aishughulikiwe kwa kifo, na walimchoma msalabani –Luka 24:20. Mungu ni mtaalamu wa kubadilisha shida nzito kuwa ushindi mkubwa. Hata hivyo, mwanadamu anatazama kila upande na laana giza lililo karibu naye. Ingawa kunaweza kuwa mfululizo wa mema murwa kwao, …mchana kwawo ni kama kivuli cha kifo… –Ayubu 24:17. Kutoa msisitizo usiofaa juu ya uovu uliotuzunguka ni kumdhihaki Mungu. Wakati sote tunaweza kutia huzuni kwa nyakati fulani mambo tuliweza kuweza kutenda au kusema tofauti, lazima tusiachi matokeo mikononi mwa Mungu. Ayubu alipitia hatima mbaya kiasi kama mtu mwingine yeyote. Hata kiasi kwamba alifungua …mdomo wake, akaaana siku yake. Na Ayubu akasema, Acha siku nisiyozaliwa ipotee, na usiku ulioambiwa, Kuna mtoto wa kiume amenakulia. Acha siku hiyo iwe giza; asimtazame Mungu juu yake, wala nuru isimulike. Acha giza na kivuli cha kifo viwekwe juu yake; acha wingu ukeeleke; acha giza la siku limuogopeshe. Kama kwa usiku huo, giza uhukumu juu yake… –Ayubu 3:1-6. Lakini mahali fulani kabla matukio hayo mabaya yalipopangwa na kuondolewa, nuru iliangaza ndani ya roho yake, naye akafuta kinywa chake na kumwabudu.

…Ajenda Binafsi

Lakini tulimtumaini yeye anayehitaji kumtumikia Israeli… –Luka 24:21. Ni jambo la kawaida kujaribu kuelewa hali yoyote iliyotolewa na wawili hawa walichagua mlinganyo sahihi. Upotovu wao ulikuwa katika kudhani jinsi Kristo angefanya hili na aina ya ukombozi walikuwa wanatafuta. Walikuwa wanatazamia siku ambayo taifa lao litainuliwa juu ya Warumi. Wakati bila kujua tunatafuta usalama wetu wenyewe, bila shaka itasababisha kukata tamaa kali. Naamani alidhani …Hakika atatoka kwangu, na kusimama, na kuomba jina la BWANA Mungu wake, na kugonga kiganja chake juu ya sehemu, na kuponya mchungaji – Wafalme wa Pili 5:11.

Abram aliahidiwa nchi ya Kanaani na aliomba kuthibitishwa. Kisha alitayarisha dhabihu ya Agano iliyoamriwa na Mungu, lakini siku yote ilipita, na Mungu hakufanya chochote nao. Na jua lilipokuwa linapozama, usingizi mzito ulinamkamata Abram; na, tazama, hofu ya giza kubwa ikamuangusha. – Mwanzo 15:12.

Wakati Abrahami alisubiri kwa Mungu ili kupokea dhabihu yake, aliendelea kupiga ndege wa mnyonyaji mbali. Lakini siku ilipokaribia mwisho alianza kujihisi ameachwa na Mungu na usiku mweusi ulianza kutulia juu ya nafsi yake. Inachukua uzoefu wa saa za kati usiku ili mambo yawe giza vya kutosha tufahamu nyota na utulivu wa kutosha kusikia sauti Yake. Lakini tulikuwa na hukumu ya kifo ndani yetu, ili tusitegemee nafsi zetu, bali Mungu ambaye huteuwa wafu –2 Wakorintho 1:9.

…Kukosa Subira

…Na juu ya yote haya, leo ni siku ya tatu tangu mambo haya yamefanyika –Luka 24:21. Wengi wetu tumefundishwa kutegemea msimu. Ni pale tumaini letu linapocheleweshwa (angalia Methali 13:12) mioyo yetu huumia na kuzini. Siku tatu zilionekana kuwa muda mrefu kwa hawa wawili. Lakini siku tatu, wiki, miezi, miaka, au hata miongo yote ni ndani ya wakati wa saa ya Mungu. Kwa muda gani utanisahau, ee BWANA? milele? kwa muda gani utaficha uso wako kwa mimi? –Zaburi 13:1.

Yusufu kwa subira alivumilia matendeleo mabaya ya ndugu zake na Potifari, lakini gereza likawa refu, naye aliomba mlimbwani asubiri kumwine atakaporejea katika hadhi yake. Lakini ilikua miaka miwili kamili (Mwanzo 41:1) hadi Farao alipoota ndoto na Yusufu hatimaye akaitwa. Lakini si kwa kosa la mlimbwani tu bali ilikuwa mapenzi ya Mungu ambaye alimwita Yusufu kupewa …kutumwa kwa chuma: Hadi wakati neno lake litakapokuja: neno la BWANA ulimjaribu –Zaburi 105:18-19. Hakuna njia bora ya kutufundisha uvumilivu zaidi ya nidhamu ya giza, ambapo wachungaji wachache wanakosa.

…Kujiudhi

Ndio, na wanawake fulani pia kati yetu walitufanya tujitazame kwa mshangao, ambao walikuwa mapema kaburini; Na walipokosa mwili wake, walikuja wakisema, kwamba pia walimuona malaika, ambao walisema kwamba yeye ni hai –Luka 24:22-23. Hakuna mtu anaye furahia kukosa. Kwa kweli, saikolojia imegundua ugonjwa mpya—FOMO (hofu ya kukosa). Habari zilizokuja kwa wanawake zilikuwa habari njema na mabadiliko ya kushangaza ya matukio, hata hivyo hakuwaletea wengine furaha kwa maana haikutokea kwao. Habari njema mara chache zinaweza kuingia kwa mtu aliyejaa kujijua mwenyewe na Eliya alikuwa mmoja wao. Usiku wake mweusi ulikuja baada ya ushindi wa kuvutia juu ya Mlima Karmeli dhidi ya wanabii wa Baali. Lakini katika giza la hisia zake binafsi …aliomba mauti; akasema, Wanaisha; sasa, ee BWANA, chukua roho yangu; kwa maana mimi si bora kuliko babu zangu –1 Wafalme 19:4.

…Hisia za Kushindwa

Na baadhi ya wale waliokuwa pamoja nasi walikwenda kaburini, na wakaiipata hiyo kama wanawake walivyosema: lakini naye hawakuona –Luka 24:24. Ni rahisi kufikiria, “Ilikuwa ikifanyia kazi kwao lakini haifanyi kazi kwangu.” Wakati jitihada zisizofanikiwa zinaweza kututia moyo, si lazima iwe kosa letu. Yohana Mbatizaji kwa uaminifu aliwahiwisha watu zuwa toba, akabatiza Kristo, na kuwa shaida wa sauti ya kulia kutoka mbinguni. Alitangaza kwa usahihi Meso wa Mkutano na kumwonyesha wale wake …Mwana Mwana wa Mungu, ambaye hutokomeza dhambi za dunia –Yohana 1:29. Ufalme huu ulimpatia nafasi salama ndani ya seli ya giza ya gereza. Alikuwa amefahamika kwa ukosefu wa faraja na mlo mdogo, lakini ilikuwa hisia ya kuachwa kabisa na Mungu ilimfikisha kwa mashaka ya giza. Na Yohana akimwingiza wawili wa wanafunzi wake, akawatuma kwa Yesu akisema, Je, wewe ndiye atakayekuja? au tunangalia mwingine? –Luka 7:19.

“Je, nilikuwa kosa?” Katika giza alianza kuishi maisha kwenye paji laini la alama ya swali. Yohana Bunyan ailielezea kama kinyesi cha kukata tamaa. Inaweza kuonekana kama D-Day kwa Mkristo, lakini msisitizo isiyofaa juu ya jitihada zetu zisizofanikiwa hapai ufufuo.

Hitimisho

Sio giza lote la kiroho linaepukika kabisa. Sio kila uzoefu wa kiroho ni wakati wa baraka za moyoni, wala si mahali popote. Kuna nyakati za mateso na majaribu yaliyokusudiwa kuleta watakatifu hadi hesabu ya nafsi ambayo ni tu usiku mweusi unaweza kutoa. Yesu mwenyewe alitemewa kwa namna inayofanana nasi, wakati katika giza lililokuwa likitawala saa ya tisa msalabani, sauti Yake ililia …kwa sauti kuu akisema, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? yaani, Mungu wangu, Mungu wangu, kwa nini umeniwacha? –Mathayo 27:46.

Barabara ya Emau inashuhudia ukweli kwamba uhai wa imani wenye nguvu hauwezi kuhakikisha kutokuwepo kwa msongo wa kiroho. Ni hadithi ya watu wa kweli wenye imani halisi wakipitia majaribu halisi. Inatusaidia kufundisha kwamba hata raha za kiroho hazipaswi kushikiliwa kwa msimamo mkubwa. Maono yetu ya kujiamini kwa ajili ya siku zijazo, sasa na kwa muda mrefu, lazima ziwe zimetobolewa katika moto wa unyenyekevu. Usiku mweusi ni mahali ambapo udanganyifu wa nafsi unaanguka, na uelewa wa karibu wa Mungu unazaliwa. Inatuleta kutoka katika kumpenda Mungu kwa sababu ya baraka anazotupatia, hadi kumpenda Mungu kwa ajili ya uhusiano wetu naye na ushirika unaofuata.

Mwenzi wa kusafiri wa Kileopa hakuwatajwa kamwe. Wengine husema alikuwa mkewe. Wengine wanadai alikuwa Luka. Lakini utambulisho wao uliachwa nje, labda ili tuweze kujaa nafasi hiyo kwa jina letu wenyewe. Maili saba kutoka Yerusalemu tunagonga ukweli wazi wa ni nani Mwokozi kweli na kwamba wokovu ni zaidi ya muhuri wa mpira unaotambulisha umiliki Wake. Mizani inatua kutoka machoni mwetu na usiku mweusi wa nafsi unatolewa kwa mwanga mkali wa saa ya mchana wa uwepo wa Mungu. Ndipo tunapokimbia kwa furaha kurudi mji wa amani tukielezwa vibaya tena. Na wakaenda na wakamwambia waliobaki: wala walikuwa wasioniaminifu –Marko 16:13.

Na hivyo, nawaza hata juu ya ufanisi wa kuandika mawazo kama haya. Si tukio linaloweza kutengenezwa au kueleweka kwa akili tu. Ni mkutano wa kibinafsi sana na Mungu na umeundwa mahsusi kwa kila mtu. Lakini labda sisi, katika kizazi chetu chenye kina kidogo, tunaweza kuhamasishwa kutanuka mikono yetu na kukumbatia giza badala ya kukutana nalo kwa chuki na upinzani. Na pale katika giza la hatari la usiku, tujifunze kukumbatia Mwokozi wa nuru.

Muda mrefu roho yangu ilikuwa gerezani,
Imefungwa kwa nguvu katika dhambi na giza la asili.
Jicho lako liliwaka miale ya kuhuisha,
Nilifungua macho; gereza likameta kwa mwanga.
Minyororo yangu ilipatikana. Moyo wangu ulikuwa huru.
Nimeamka, nikatoka, na nikikutekelea.

- Charles Wesley

This is the first of a series of articles on “Discipleship.” Today, Jesus is continuing to call men and women to respond to the simple call, “Follow Me.” Jesus is calling each of us to personally “Follow Me.” In this series, we will explore the depth of this simple command of Jesus. Like the disciples, you will find yourself drawn to follow Jesus.

You may experience both exhilaration and apprehension. Exhilaration, as your journey of faith takes you to heights of love that you have never known. Apprehension, as your faith is tested in new and difficult ways.

There is an emptiness in every human heart that only Jesus can fill. There is a purity and beauty in the life of Jesus that resonates with those heart longings. As we walk with Jesus, we find ourselves being transformed. Old things pass away. All things become new. His life becomes our life. His desires become our desires.

Discipleship is incumbent on the believer. Believing in Jesus, repenting of our sins, and receiving the Lord Jesus into our heart are the first steps into a lifelong journey of faith. Discipleship is not an alternate means of salvation. Following Jesus is the response of a soul set free. Following Jesus is not a carnal attempt to merit eternal life. It is the love response of one who has discovered the source of life.

If you join us on this journey, you will discover that following Jesus will lead us into the valley of decision where we will find ourselves compelled to choose between a life of total surrender to Christ or a life of sin and pleasing self.

And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men. And they straightway left their nets, and followed him. And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them. And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him –Matthew 4:18-22.

Imagine yourself in a ship with one of these brethren. The sun was rising on the eastern horizon. Anticipating another day of fishing the blue waters of the Galilee, you busy yourself with the daily tasks. Fishing has been your life. You are as much at home on the sea as you are in your cottage.

Another day, another catch of fish, and you should be able to keep the creditors at bay for another week. It’s the only life you have ever known. Your father was a fisherman. Your grandfather was a fisherman. It’s a comfortable life. It’s a familiar life.

This morning, as the waves are gently lapping the sandy shoreline, a man approaches. He’s not a total stranger. Everyone knows about Mary’s son. Everyone has an opinion about Mary’s son. He astounds the local rabbi with his knowledge of the scriptures. His character is flawless; He is the friend of all and a stranger to none.

This man, Jesus (that is his name) is drawing near to your ship. As He draws near, He calls out in a rather cheerful voice, “Follow me.”

James looks at John, and together they look to their father Zebedee. His approving nod was all that they needed. Zebedee had worked with his two sons for many years. Perhaps he was hoping that time with the Nazarene would soften the temper of their abrasive characters.

“Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.” That’s what He called out to Peter and Andrew. They left their little boat full of nets, perhaps tethered to a stump by the shore. What was it about this Man that He could draw disciples after Him with a simple “Follow Me”? Maybe it was a deep longing in the heart of these disciples—a “hope” that following Jesus might fulfill.

Generations of Jewish men had been looking for The Messiah—The Promised One; He who would break the Roman yoke and restore Israel to her former freedom and glory. Jesus was the most promising revolutionary prospect of the day. He would need a following. He would need their help. Little did they realize that day as they dropped their nets and followed Jesus where that journey would lead them. Little did they know that if they followed this Man, they would never be the same.

As Peter, Andrew, James, and John joined with eight others to follow Jesus, they were walking away from the familiar, secure life of the fisherman. They may have thought that following Jesus would be an adventure. They may have thought that after a term of service to the Nazarene, they could return to their fishing boats. As a matter of fact, that is what they did.

After Jesus’ crucifixion and resurrection, He made several appearances to His disciples. They had not yet received the Holy Spirit, and, in the midst of this great uncertainty, they could not resist the allure of the familiar. They decided to go fishing, but much to their consternation they had lost the touch. They fished all night and caught nothing. In the morning Jesus was standing on the shore. He told them to cast on the right side of the ship. They cast and were not able to pull in the nets due to the multitude of fish.

Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing. But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus. Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No. And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes –John 21:3-6.

Have you ever found yourself in a position where you have tried and tried and all your efforts are met with failure? You know what it is to “reach the end of my hoarded resources”. If that is where you find yourself, you are in a position to experience a miracle. God shows himself strong to those who acknowledge their weakness.

When you decide to follow Jesus, He will draw you into such an utter dependence upon Him that you will finally no longer trust in yourself. To become truly like Jesus is to realize with Paul …that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing…. Paul then continues the verse …for to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not –Romans 7:18.

Discipleship will lead us into a total abandonment of ourselves to Christ. Just as the disciples could not have fathomed where following Jesus would lead them, neither can we. We make a faith choice. We choose to follow. We commit the details to our Master.

If you want to be like Jesus, you cannot look back. Jesus said: …No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God –Luke 9:62. Peter looked back. He said, “I go a fishing”. Disillusioned following the crucifixion and glorious resurrection, Peter chose to return to the lifestyle that was familiar to him. He went back to fishing and James and John went with him.

When Jesus appeared on the shore after their long night of fruitless toil, He prepared a fish fry for the weary disciples. As Peter sat munching on a charbroiled fish, Jesus turned to him and said, “Peter, do you love Me more than these?” How gently piercing are the words of Jesus.

Peter responded, “Yes Lord, you know that I love you.” Jesus said, “Feed my lambs.” We do not know how much time passed, but Jesus turned to him again, “Peter…” (actually He called him Simon) “Do you love Me?” Peter gave the same staid response. “Yes Lord, you know that I love you”. It was the right answer, but Jesus was interested in more than just a right answer, so He said to him again, “Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou Me?”

Peter finally began to feel that Jesus was asking for something more of him—something that pierced his soul through and through. He had begun following Jesus with the desire to receive from Him. Now Jesus is asking him to reciprocate that love.

Scenes of Caiaphas’ house came before him. He saw Jesus being brutally handled, falsely accused, and spat upon. He heard the angry shouting of the Sanhedrin as they called for Jesus’ death. And then there was that persistent young damsel that challenged him that he was one of Jesus’ disciples. He said to her, “I am not”. Three times he had denied knowing Jesus and now three times Jesus has challenged his love.

In anguish of heart Peter cried out, “Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee”. Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep”. From that day, Peter was a man with a calling, not only to know Christ for the purpose of receiving from him, but also to emulate him. Discipleship is more than merely knowing about Jesus. Discipleship is walking in his footsteps and identifying with Jesus in his ministry and in his sufferings—truly knowing Him.

Jesus is asking you today, “Do you love me?” We all know the right answer, “Yes, of course, I love Jesus.” Then “Love your neighbor” – “Serve the needy” – “Defer to your brother” – “Forgive the one that has offended you”.

Discipleship is very practical in that it moves us beyond the ideological and causes us to become the very hands and feet of Jesus to those around us.

If in your heart you are thinking, this doesn’t sound very appealing, I would encourage you to focus on the moment and the task at hand. Peter walked with Jesus for three and a half years before he received this call from Jesus. Jesus never calls us without equipping us, and He doesn’t equip us until He determines that we are ready. After the Day of Pentecost, Peter was called, he was prepared, and he was equipped. Then God used him mightily to establish the church.

I would like to call your attention to another attribute of discipleship that is sometimes misplaced. Discipleship is never intended to be drudgery. If you find following Jesus to be hard and toilsome, that is evidence that your love has not yet been perfected.

Jesus’ soul-piercing question to Peter was quite simple, “Do you love Me?” It was as if Jesus was testing Peter. [“I have a job for you, Peter, but a prerequisite for this job is your devoted love for Me.”] Discipleship is a love response to Jesus. Our love for Christ makes service a joy. Toil is pleasant and sacrifice is not a loss.

We can best understand this in the context of human relationships. If you are married and you truly love your husband or your wife, you do not even consider it a sacrifice to work for the mutual benefit of your marriage. In the same way, if we are truly in love with Jesus it is not considered toil to work for him. No sacrifice that we make for the kingdom of heaven is a loss.

I welcome you to join us as we explore the realities of discipleship. We will learn from Christ’s example of forgiveness. We will gain a greater understanding of what it means to walk by faith. Jesus taught us to not worry but to trust. He taught lessons on servant leadership and on cross bearing. There is so much to discover when we are walking with Jesus.

Expect to be changed. The teachings of Jesus are revolutionary in that they run counter to our human impulses. Purpose to allow the life of Christ to become your life and you will be amazed by what God will do for you.
