When you, my friend, are standing on this earth
And gazing up into the firmament
Where stretches all of space, what do you see?
A great black blanket stretched o’er all the sky
With many a mystery light somewhere up there?
Or can you see the distances so great
Which stretch the mind almost to breaking point
And make you feel the size you really are?
In the still silence of the spacious sky,
The far-off planets seem almost in reach
Compared to the great distance to the stars.
The crescent moon is closer yet to you,
And yet it took man three whole days to reach
That tiny sphere so very close at hand.
But what you see while gazing up to heights
Which you cannot begin to comprehend
Is but a streak of all the vast expanse
Beyond the knowledge of this human race.
And so, my friend, I hope that you will feel
That greatness, vastness, emptiness of space
Which our Creator made for us so we
Can feel His greatness and His tender love
And humbly bow our heads and worship Him.

–by Daniel Kaufman

It’s been said that in the 1500s, after baptism, the Anabaptists lived an average of only 27 days. They were hunted and killed. They realized one thing—serving Christ would most certainly cost them everything. They forsook the comforts of easy living; they forsook it all. It could also have been a similar situation when Jesus walked on the earth, or shortly after He was killed.

…and he turned, and said unto them, If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple. For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish. Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple –Luke 14:25-33.

Jesus clearly asked His disciples to count the cost. And they must have counted the cost, for they faithfully gave all, including their lives, for Christ’s Kingdom. They realized they could have had the good things in this life; however, they also realized it would cost them the good things in the next.

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution –2 Timothy 3:12. If we look at the promises which Jesus gave us in His Word about persecution, and then compare them with the lives of Jesus’ followers today, we might be confused. And rightfully so.

He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked –1 John 2:6. Jesus says we should walk as He walked, He also tells us that we need to follow Him.

How did He walk? We know that Jesus had no place to lay His head—this was how He wanted it. We know that Jesus could have chosen to live where and how He wanted. He was, in fact, in control of the whole world, yet He was despised and rejected by the world and its system. When He spoke, people wanted to lay their hands on Him; they wanted to kill Him. He was not a popular person; He had few friends. In reality, He didn’t fit in, and He didn’t last long. Three years after His ministry began, He was killed. …He was numbered with the transgressors –Mark 15:28.

What about His followers today? Are they walking how He walked? And if not, why not?

We read about the children of Israel going through the wilderness. They fought and overtook the cities in their paths, killing all in the process. We read many accounts about how God instructed the children of Israel to kill all of the enemy, even the women and children. The following is one such account of many.

So the LORD our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining. And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many. And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city –Deuteronomy 3:3-6.

We read accounts like this in scripture, and it can cause us to cringe. It is almost as if life itself was not important. Even in the New Testament, death doesn’t seem to be that big of a deal. People lived and people died.

The first week after we moved to Haiti, I was driving through the city. Suddenly, right in front of me I saw a man lying in the street. Blood ran down the road and pooled in a low spot—he was dead. I was shocked. But what shocked me the most was that no one seemed to notice. People by the hundreds busily walked around him, not even looking at the man—no one cared.

Over the next six years we saw many dead or dying people—it became a normal scene.

If that was how it was back in the Bible times, and it is still how it is today in many countries of the world, maybe we are the ones that are out of the norm? Maybe we esteem life higher than God does. Maybe we are among those that Jesus spoke of when He said—He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal –John 12:25.

In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:19. We were created out of the dust, and after a few short years, we return to the very same dust.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –James 4:14. The Bible also calls our lives a vapor.

We all know what happens after that—the judgment, then eternity. So why do we care so much about this life? Maybe it is an American problem or a western problem.

It is obvious that Americans are looked upon as ‘more valuable’ than most other nationalities. If you are an American in a developing country, you are heralded as a king. If something happens to an American, it is quickly headline news. I once stood over the bodies of two murdered men. One of their close friends stood by, so I asked him how he was doing. He shrugged and said, “This is life”.

So why does life mean so much to us Americans? The answer is simple. We can obtain almost anything we want; money is easy to get, and we can live how we want. We can live in pleasure every day. We go to the store and buy what we want, when we want—we have it our way. This is just how it is; for most of us it is all we have ever known—the life of plenty. So how does this affect us?

This type of living makes it especially hard to ‘give all’ for Christ. It makes it difficult to obey Jesus’ command to …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15. It makes it difficult to say with the Apostle Paul, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. In reality, it makes it difficult to be a Christian.

When Jesus said… For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25, what did He mean? Could it mean literally just what it says: that when you fall in love with your own life, you cannot effectively follow Christ, so that in the end you will actually lose your life?

Can you go to the lost and forsake the comforts of this life if it’s those comforts that you love and live for? It’s not likely. What we have is “Americanized” Christians that will only go to the mission field if they can take their comforts with them. This produces rich, comfortable missionaries who, despite their best efforts, can’t win the lost, rather they make them jealous. Can we go into the cities and preach the gospel to the lost like so many before us have? Can we take time to teach and disciple the tens of thousands who are seeking? If we love our lives, we probably will not, since there is too much to lose and it’s a waste of good talent and opportunity. God help us.

When we are living to please the flesh and we have our lives figured out, it is hard for God to use us. We are puffed up. We tend to believe that God has blessed us because of all our possessions and our status in life; but isn’t this the prosperity gospel? What if that changed? Would we still consider ourselves to be blessed? Is it God or our own doing that causes us to be joyful? What if we found ourselves in John the Baptist’s shoes? Or the Apostle Paul’s? If we would be sitting in prison for doing nothing wrong, would our joy remain? It should if the Holy Spirit is living and working in our hearts. The Bible says that we can suffer joyfully!

Years ago, a coworker of mine was a happy fellow. He had a nice life. There was one problem—he did not believe there was a God. We would talk day after day. He would constantly tell me how happy he was and that one didn’t need to be a Christian to be happy. He would talk about his nice life, all that he possessed, his good job, his nice family. Interestingly enough, he truly did seem happy.

I would tell him that true happiness didn’t come from the things that we possess or the position that we find ourselves in, but he would just disagree. He also proclaimed that he lived a better life than most Christians that he knew. He also said he didn’t get angry like most Christians and could control himself. I tried to convince him that he was deceived. At times I would think I was getting somewhere with him, then later it would seem I was far from reaching him. One day he soberly admitted that I seemed to be different that most Christians he had known in the past, but that still wasn’t enough.

I left that job and lost contact with him. Recently, I ran into another one of my former coworkers. I quickly thought of my friend and asked how he was doing. He looked at me strangely and then shocked me to my core as he said, “He committed suicide”.

The devil wants us to love our life—it’s that simple. When we love our life, we focus on it, we cherish it. The last thing we want to do is lose our life, even if it is for something eternal.

When I was in the Marines, they would constantly remind us that our lives were not number one; our country was. There are many young men who put their country first. Many have gone and given their all; many have died.

In World War 2, the Japanese would try to sneak up to a fox hole housing soldiers and throw in a grenade. Many times, it didn’t end like the Japanese wanted, because someone would jump on the grenade, absorbing the explosion. Thousands gave their lives to save their friends and defend their country. But be sure, if their priorities were not in order (of country first before themselves), they would not have done so.

If someone today, in America, would risk their life for the sake of the gospel, he would be labeled as foolish, reckless, and immature. But what do we say about so many before us—the ones that gave their lives while standing for the same things that we say we believe today? And what about the thousands today who are putting their lives on the line in other countries—are they foolish? Let’s look at a very obvious example in Acts.

And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus. And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem. Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. –Acts 21:10-13.

What would we think of Paul’s actions today? Paul went to Jerusalem and was quickly taken, beaten, and put in prison. It was the beginning of the end for our dear brother. He was moved from prison to prison and eventually ended up in Rome where he was beheaded. What do you think the ones that tried to persuade him to not go to Jerusalem thought? Do you think they called him a fool? Did they shake their heads and say, “I told him not to go!”?

We cannot know for sure. However, I am sure that Paul was simply putting the kingdom of Christ first; his life did not matter. He was obeying God, and God had told him to go.

When we love our lives, it is very difficult to be an effective disciple of the Lord Jesus. We end up forsaking God’s calling and then we are stuck trying to live the Christian life alone, and without God—no spiritual help from above, causing us to fall way short of the mark.

It’s ironic that only when we forsake all, including our lives, will we find true peace and purpose for our lives. And when we love our lives, that is when we will lose them.

Rise up, O saints of God!
Have done with lesser things.
Give heart and soul and mind and strength
To serve the King of kings.

Rise up, O saints of God!
The kingdom tarries long.
Bring in the day of Christlike love
And end the night of wrong.

Lift high the cross of Christ!
Tread where His feet have trod.
Led onward by the Son of Man,
Rise up, O saints of God!

Let us rise up, as God’s people, and begin to be done with lesser things, with our gaze on things above, not on the things of this earth. Yes, we will stand out; we will be labeled fools and many other things. However, we will once again catch God’s attention and the fires of revival will once again burn!

Dizem que, nos anos 1500, depois do batismo, os anabatistas viviam, em média, apenas 27 dias. Eram perseguidos e mortos. Eles perceberam uma coisa — servir a Cristo certamente lhes custaria tudo. Eles renunciaram aos confortos de uma vida fácil; renunciaram a tudo. Poderia também ter sido uma situação semelhante quando Jesus andou sobre a terra, ou logo depois de Ele ter sido morto.

…e, voltando ele, disse-lhes: Se alguém vem a mim e não aborrece de seu pai, e mãe, e mulher, e filhos, e irmãos, e irmãs, e ainda própria a sua vida, não pode ser meu discípulo. E qualquer que não leva a sua cruz e não vem após mim, não pode ser meu discípulo. Pois qual dentre vós, querendo edificar uma torre, não se senta primeiro e calcula o custo, se tem com que a acabar? Para que, depois, havendo lançado o fundamento e não podendo acabar, todos os que o virem não comecem a escarnecer dele, dizendo: Este homem começou a edificar e não pôde acabar. Ou qual rei dentre vós, indo fazer guerra contra outro rei, não se assenta primeiro e consulta se com dez mil pode resistir ao que vem contra ele com vinte mil? Ou, estando ainda longe, manda uma embaixada e trata de condições de paz? Assim, qualquer de vós que não renuncia a tudo o que tem, não pode ser meu discípulo –Lucas 14:25-33.

Jesus claramente pediu aos Seus discípulos que calculassem o custo. E eles devem ter calculado o custo, pois deram fielmente tudo, inclusive suas vidas, pelo Reino de Cristo. Eles perceberam que poderiam ter as coisas boas desta vida; entretanto, também perceberam que isso lhes custaria as coisas boas da próxima.

E, na verdade, todos os que querem viver piedosamente em Cristo Jesus padecerão perseguições –2 Timóteo 3:12. Se olharmos para as promessas que Jesus nos deu em Sua Palavra sobre a perseguição, e então as compararmos com a vida dos seguidores de Jesus hoje, podemos ficar confusos. E com razão.

Aquele que diz que permanece nele também deve andar assim como ele andou –1 João 2:6. Jesus diz que devemos andar como Ele andou; Ele também nos diz que precisamos segui‑lo.

Como Ele andou? Sabemos que Jesus não tinha onde reclinar a cabeça — assim foi que Ele quis. Sabemos que Jesus poderia ter escolhido viver onde e como quisesse. Ele estava, de fato, no controle de todo o mundo, contudo foi desprezado e rejeitado pelo mundo e pelo seu sistema. Quando falou, as pessoas quiseram apanhá‑lo; quiseram matá‑lo. Ele não era uma pessoa popular; tinha poucos amigos. Na realidade, Ele não se encaixava, e não durou muito. Três anos depois do início de Seu ministério, Ele foi morto. …Ele foi contado entre os transgressores –Marcos 15:28.

E quanto aos Seus seguidores hoje? Eles estão andando como Ele andou? E, se não, por que não?

Lemos sobre os filhos de Israel passando pelo deserto. Eles lutavam e tomavam as cidades em seu caminho, matando todos no processo. Lemos muitos relatos de como Deus instruiu os filhos de Israel a matar todos os inimigos, até as mulheres e crianças. O seguinte é um desses relatos entre muitos.

Assim o SENHOR nosso Deus entregou nas nossas mãos também Og, rei de Basã, e todo o seu povo; e o ferimos, até que nenhum lhe ficou remanescente. E àquele tempo tomamos todas as suas cidades; não havia cidade que não tomássemos deles, sessenta cidades, toda a região de Argobe, o reino de Og, em Basã. Todas essas cidades eram fortificadas com muros altos, portas e cadeados; além das cidades sem muro em grande número. E destruímo‑las por completo, como a Sião, rei de Hesbom, destruindo por completo os homens, as mulheres e as crianças de cada cidade –Deuteronômio 3:3-6.

Lemos relatos assim nas Escrituras, e isso pode nos fazer estremecer. Parece quase como se a própria vida não fosse importante. Mesmo no Novo Testamento, a morte não parece ser algo tão grande. As pessoas viviam e as pessoas morriam.

Na primeira semana depois que nos mudamos para o Haiti, eu dirigia pela cidade. De repente, bem à minha frente, vi um homem deitado na rua. Sangue corria pela estrada e se acumulava em um ponto baixo — ele estava morto. Fiquei chocado. Mas o que mais me chocou foi que ninguém parecia notar. Centenas de pessoas caminhavam ocupadas ao redor dele, sem sequer olhar para o homem — ninguém se importava.

Nos seis anos que se seguiram vimos muitas pessoas mortas ou moribundas — tornou‑se uma cena normal.

Se era assim nos tempos bíblicos, e ainda é assim hoje em muitos países do mundo, talvez sejamos nós os que estamos fora do comum? Talvez estimemos a vida mais do que Deus a estima. Talvez estejamos entre aqueles de quem Jesus falou quando disse — Aquele que ama a sua vida a perderá; e o que aborrece a sua vida neste mundo a conservará para a vida eterna –João 12:25.

Com o suor do teu rosto comerás o teu pão, até que te tornes à terra, porquanto dela foste tomado; porquanto és pó e em pó te tornarás –Gênesis 3:19. Fomos criados do pó, e depois de alguns anos breves, voltamos ao mesmo pó.

Vós não sabeis o que será amanhã. Pois que é a vossa vida? É um vapor que aparece por um pouco e depois se desvanece –Tiago 4:14. A Bíblia também chama a nossa vida de vapor.

Todos sabemos o que acontece depois disso — o juízo, e então a eternidade. Então por que nos importamos tanto com esta vida? Talvez seja um problema americano ou ocidental.

É óbvio que os americanos são vistos como “mais valiosos” do que a maioria das outras nacionalidades. Se você é americano em um país em desenvolvimento, é saudado como um rei. Se algo acontece com um americano, isso rapidamente vira notícia principal. Certa vez fiquei sobre os corpos de dois homens assassinados. Um dos seus amigos próximos ficou ao lado; então perguntei como ele estava. Ele deu de ombros e disse: “Isto é a vida”.

Então por que a vida significa tanto para nós, americanos? A resposta é simples. Podemos obter quase tudo o que queremos; o dinheiro é fácil de conseguir, e podemos viver como queremos. Podemos viver no prazer todos os dias. Vamos à loja e compramos o que queremos, quando queremos — temos do nosso jeito. Assim é; para a maioria de nós é tudo o que já conhecemos — a vida de abundância. Então como isso nos afeta?

Esse tipo de vida torna especialmente difícil “dar tudo” por Cristo. Torna difícil obedecer ao mandamento de Jesus de …Ide por todo o mundo e pregai o evangelho a toda criatura –Marcos 16:15. Torna difícil dizer com o apóstolo Paulo, Para mim o viver é Cristo, e o morrer é ganho –Filipenses 1:21. Na realidade, torna difícil ser cristão.

Quando Jesus disse… Porque qualquer que quiser salvar a sua vida a perderá; mas qualquer que perder a sua vida por amor de mim a achará –Mateus 16:25, o que quis dizer? Poderia significar literalmente exatamente o que diz: que quando você se apaixona pela sua própria vida, não pode seguir Cristo eficazmente, de modo que, no fim, você realmente perderá a vida?

Pode você ir aos perdidos e renunciar aos confortos desta vida se são esses confortos que você ama e para os quais vive? Isso não é provável. O que temos são cristãos “americanizados” que só irão ao campo missionário se puderem levar seus confortos com eles. Isso produz missionários ricos e confortáveis que, apesar de seus melhores esforços, não conseguem ganhar os perdidos; ao contrário, tornam‑nos invejosos. Podemos ir às cidades e pregar o evangelho aos perdidos como tantos antes de nós o fizeram? Podemos dedicar tempo para ensinar e discipular as dezenas de milhares que estão buscando? Se amamos nossas vidas, provavelmente não faremos, pois há muito a perder e seria um desperdício de talento e oportunidade. Deus nos ajude.

Quando vivemos para agradar a carne e achamos que temos a vida resolvida, é difícil para Deus nos usar. Estamos empolgados de orgulho. Tendemos a crer que Deus nos abençoou por causa de todas as nossas posses e do nosso status na vida; mas isso não é o evangelho da prosperidade? E se isso mudasse? Ainda nos consideraríamos abençoados? É Deus ou obra nossa que nos causa alegria? E se nos encontrássemos no lugar de João Batista? Ou do apóstolo Paulo? Se estivéssemos na prisão por não ter feito nada de errado, nossa alegria permaneceria? Deveria, se o Espírito Santo vive e opera em nossos corações. A Bíblia diz que podemos sofrer com alegria!

Anos atrás, um colega meu era uma pessoa feliz. Tinha uma boa vida. Havia um problema — ele não acreditava que havia um Deus. Conversávamos dia após dia. Ele constantemente me dizia o quão feliz era e que não se precisava ser cristão para ser feliz. Falava de sua boa vida, de tudo o que possuía, de seu bom emprego, de sua família amável. Curiosamente, ele realmente parecia feliz.

Eu lhe dizia que a verdadeira felicidade não vinha das coisas que possuímos ou da posição em que nos encontramos, mas ele simplesmente discordava. Também proclamava que vivia melhor do que a maioria dos cristãos que conhecia. Acrescentava que não se irritava como a maioria dos cristãos e que sabia se controlar. Tentei convencê‑lo de que estava enganado. Às vezes achava que estava chegando a algum lugar com ele, mas depois parecia que estava longe de alcançá‑lo. Um dia ele admitiu seriamente que eu parecia diferente da maioria dos cristãos que ele conhecera no passado, mas isso ainda não era suficiente.

Saí daquele emprego e perdi contato com ele. Recentemente, encontrei outro antigo colega de trabalho. Pensei rapidamente no meu amigo e perguntei como ele estava. Ele olhou para mim estranhamente e então me chocou profundamente ao dizer: “Ele cometeu suicídio”.

O diabo quer que amemos a nossa vida — é simples assim. Quando amamos nossa vida, focamos nela, a estimamos. A última coisa que queremos é perder nossa vida, mesmo que seja por algo eterno.

Quando eu estava nos Fuzileiros Navais, eles constantemente nos lembravam que nossas vidas não eram a coisa mais importante; nosso país era. Muitos jovens colocam seu país em primeiro lugar. Muitos partiram e deram tudo; muitos morreram.

Na Segunda Guerra Mundial, os japoneses tentavam aproximar‑se sorrateiramente de uma trincheira onde soldados estavam e lançar uma granada. Muitas vezes, não acabou como os japoneses queriam, porque alguém pulava sobre a granada, absorvendo a explosão. Milhares deram suas vidas para salvar seus amigos e defender seu país. Mas tenha certeza: se suas prioridades não estivessem na ordem certa (o país em primeiro lugar antes de si mesmos), eles não o teriam feito.

Se alguém hoje, na América, arriscasse sua vida por causa do evangelho, seria rotulado de tolo, imprudente e imaturo. Mas o que dizer de tantos antes de nós — aqueles que deram suas vidas enquanto defendiam as mesmas coisas que hoje dizemos crer? E quanto aos milhares hoje que estão pondo suas vidas em risco em outros países — são eles tolos? Vejamos um exemplo muito óbvio em Atos.

E, estando nós ali por vários dias, desceu da Judeia um certo profeta, chamado Ágabo. E, vindo ter conosco, tomou o cinto de Paulo e amarrou as mãos e os pés, e disse: Assim diz o Espírito Santo: Assim atarão em Jerusalém o homem a quem pertence este cinto, e o entregarão nas mãos dos gentios. E, ouvindo nós isso, tanto nós como os que dali estavam rogávamos a ele que não subisse a Jerusalém. Então Paulo lhes disse: Que é, pois, que estais chorando e quebrantando o meu coração? Porque estou pronto não só a ser preso, mas também a morrer em Jerusalém pelo nome do Senhor Jesus –Atos 21:10-13.

O que pensaríamos das ações de Paulo hoje? Paulo foi a Jerusalém e logo foi preso, espancado e encarcerado. Foi o começo do fim para nosso caro irmão. Foi movido de uma prisão a outra e, eventualmente, acabou em Roma, onde foi decapitado. O que vocês acham que pensaram aqueles que tentaram persuadi‑lo a não ir a Jerusalém? Acham que o chamaram de tolo? Sacudiram a cabeça e disseram: “Eu disse‑lhe para não ir!”?

Não podemos saber ao certo. Contudo, tenho certeza de que Paulo estava simplesmente pondo o reino de Cristo em primeiro lugar; sua vida não importava. Ele estava obedecendo a Deus, e Deus lhe disse para ir.

Quando amamos nossas vidas, é muito difícil ser um discípulo eficaz do Senhor Jesus. Acabamos por renunciar ao chamado de Deus e então ficamos presos tentando viver a vida cristã sozinhos e sem Deus — sem ajuda espiritual do alto, fazendo com que fiquemos muito aquém da meta.

É irônico que só quando renunciamos a tudo, inclusive às nossas vidas, encontraremos a verdadeira paz e propósito para nossa existência. E quando amamos nossas vidas, é então que as perderemos.

Levantai‑vos, ó santos de Deus!
Acabai com coisas menores.
Dai coração e alma e mente e força
Para servir ao Rei dos reis.

Levantai‑vos, ó santos de Deus!
O reino tarda a chegar.
Trazei o dia do amor semelhante ao de Cristo
E encerrai a noite do mal.

Erguei alto a cruz de Cristo!
Ponde os pés onde Ele pisou.
Conduzidos pelo Filho do Homem,
Levantai‑vos, ó santos de Deus!

Levantemo‑nos, como povo de Deus, e comecemos a nos afastar das coisas menores, com nosso olhar nas coisas do alto, não nas coisas desta terra. Sim, nos destacaremos; seremos rotulados de tolos e muitas outras coisas. Entretanto, voltaremos a chamar a atenção de Deus e os fogos do avivamento novamente arderão!

And he said unto them, What manner of communications are these
that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad? –Luke 24:17.

On June 6, 1944, 156,000 American, British, and Canadian troops landed on a 50-mile stretch of beach in Normandy, France. After several months of intense fighting, they overcame the initial defenses and swarmed into the German-held territory. The surprise attack, known as D-Day, caught the Germans off guard. However, it wasn’t until March of the next year that France was finally liberated from German forces. D-day was the beginning of the end of World War II on the western front and it was the event that seemed to sap the life from the notorious German army, from which they never recovered. It appears rather coincidental that so many words with a negative connotation begin with the letter D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

I can imagine that these two believers, plodding upon the road to Emmaus that dim and dismal evening, were feeling a little the same way. Their D-Day had arrived totally unexpected. I would suspect that every living person has at one time or another experienced moments of intense sadness—their own D-day, so-to-speak. Even some animals have been known to express a melancholy mood at the death of their master or mate. But these two disciples seemed to be experiencing a pain far beyond the normal loss of a friend. They were staring into the face of the grim reality that all their bright hopes of a shining tomorrow were hopelessly shattered in a ruinous heap at the foot of the cross.

This agony was no ordinary fit of depression but rather it was a depression linked to a crisis of faith. This type of discouragement is a state of intense spiritual anguish in which the struggling, despairing believer feels he is abandoned by God. It is a hopeless feeling that the sun of God's blessedness has been eclipsed and the dark night of the soul has become a permanent resident within.

While all of us seek to valiantly resist such dark temptations, a brief search into the lives of many godly men will reveal that these temptations are very real and are quite common to man. In such a condition, life seems impossible and the impending gloom that has settled upon the heart sees no light at the end of the tunnel. Why is my pain perpetual, and my wound incurable, which refuseth to be healed? wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail? –Jeremiah 15:18. This is obviously an overstated exaggeration that escaped the lips of the weeping prophet, but it gives us a direct snapshot into the dreaded pain in the depths of his soul.

For we would not, brethren, have you ignorant of our trouble which came to us in Asia, that we were pressed out of measure, above strength, insomuch that we despaired even of life: But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:8-9. This dark night of the soul shows no respect to persons. It invades the lives of princes and paupers, preachers and penitents, public and private people, pulpits and pews. These two disciples had verbally revisited every possible scenario in their journey along the Emmaus Road. They had no doubt found plenty of fault in others as well as personal regret. The “what ifs” and “if onlys” had thoroughly been discussed, but nothing could reverse the outcome and their restless anxiety lingered still.

The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus was about threescore furlongs or approximately seven miles. And along this doleful journey a Stranger joined ranks with the distraught duo in their D-Day and asked them for an account of their sadness. But he is no curious onlooker. He is the risen Lord who has come to cast His heavenly light upon our darkened pathway. Rather than revealing Himself abruptly, and perhaps for our benefit, he patiently allows them to expose the depleted spiritual road that they were treading upon.

Thus, the conversation unfolds as the mile markers pass, each revealing our sincere erroneous efforts that lead us further from the city of peace and into the dark night of the soul…

…The Ignorance of Others

And the one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering said unto him, Art thou only a stranger in Jerusalem, and hast not known the things which are come to pass there in these days? –Luke 24:18. Ask any stranger on the streets of New York City why the flags were flying at half-mast three days after the towers fell on September 11, and you would receive the same incredulous answer ascribed to these two. “How can you be so ignorant?” We all tend to marvel at people who do not hold the same knowledge that we imagine ourselves to possess. The younger the man, the more answers that he believes the coffers of his understanding hold.

This is nothing new. Moses, as a young man, …supposed his brethren would have understood how that God by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not –Acts 7:25. While he firmly understood that he owned the plan of God, he was badly mistaken in the percentage that he possessed. If our recourse cannot rectify the given situation, our answers are not the real answer. The heartfelt disdain that naturally arises toward those who see it differently is the beginning marker that we are on the wrong path. Miles down the pathway of life, Moses began to feel the desperation of that pain and the darkness of the hour. I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. And if thou deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee, out of hand, if I have found favour in thy sight; and let me not see my wretchedness –Numbers 11:14-15. Why did Moses not see this earlier in life? For the same cause that these two fervent disciples’ …eyes were holden that they should not know him –Luke 24:16.

…Reason

And he said unto them, What things? And they said unto him, Concerning Jesus of Nazareth, which was a prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people –Luke 24:19. They had their private perception of who the Christ was, but they were seeing …through a glass, darkly… –1 Corinthians 13:12. Their partial knowledge was leaning heavily on their own understanding and looking for the wrong kind of redemption. To them, their redeemer was (past tense) a prophet that no longer could do what they wanted him to do. We all want Jesus to solve our problems and make us feel better, but His purpose is to free us from our presumption and sin.

Jacob had every reason to believe that the birthright and blessing was to be his. At Bethel, God had promised to bless him. Jacob reckoned this to arrive in a material format. And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me, and will keep me in this way that I go, and will give me bread to eat, and raiment to put on, So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God –Genesis 28:20-21.

But the greatest blessing he ever received from God arrived to him on the wings of a deep dark night. And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day. And when he saw that he prevailed not against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and the hollow of Jacob's thigh was out of joint, as he wrestled with him. And he said, Let me go, for the day breaketh. And he said, I will not let thee go, except thou bless me. And he said unto him, What is thy name? And he said, Jacob. And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for as a prince hast thou power with God and with men, and hast prevailed –Genesis 32:24-28.

Jacob had already accumulated an abundance of earthly possessions. What more could he want? It was a dark night for Jacob when he discovered that he’d spent his life pursuing possessions and resisting God. He now seeks godly character and spiritual affluence. His victory was through surrender, and he limped away as a cripple with a crown. The Lord cannot fully bless a man until He has first conquered his powers of reason.

…Ill Fate

And how the chief priests and our rulers delivered him to be condemned to death, and have crucified him –Luke 24:20. God specializes in turning grave dilemmas into monumental victories. Still, man looks around him and curses the darkness about him. Though there may be a volley of good reciprocating them, …the morning is to them even as the shadow of death… –Job 24:17. To give undo emphasis upon the evil about us is to mock the divinity of God. While we all may regret at times things that we could have done or said differently, we must invariably leave the results in the hands of God. Job experienced as much ill fate as anybody. So much so that he opened …his mouth, and cursed his day. And Job spake, and said, Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived. Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it. Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it. As for that night, let darkness seize upon it… –Job 3:1-6. But somewhere before the dark events were rectified and lifted, the light shined into his soul, and he laid his hand to his mouth and worshiped.

…Personal Agenda

But we trusted that it had been he which should have redeemed Israel… –Luke 24:21. It is but natural to attempt to understand any given situation and these two had selected the correct equation. Their folly lay in the presumption of the means that Christ was to perform this and the type of redemption they were to receive. They were looking forward to the day when their nation would be exalted over the Romans. When we unwittingly seek our own security, it is bound to lead to bitter disappointment. Naaman thought …He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper –2 Kings 5:11.

Abraham was promised the land of Canaan and he asked for a confirmation. He then prepared the covenant sacrifice prescribed by God, but the entire day passed, and God did nothing with them. And when the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram; and, lo, an horror of great darkness fell upon him. –Genesis 15:12.

As Abraham waited on God to receive his offering, he continued to beat back the birds of prey. But as the day neared an end he began to feel abandoned by God and the dark night began to settle upon his soul. It takes a midnight experience for things to get dark enough for us to see the stars and quiet enough to hear His voice. But we had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God which raiseth the dead –2 Corinthians 1:9.

…Impatience

…And beside all this, to day is the third day since these things were done –Luke 24:21. Many of us are disciplined enough to hold out for a season. It is when our hope is deferred (see Proverbs 13:12) that our hearts grow sick and faint. Three days seemed like a long time to these two. But three days, weeks, months, years, or even decades are all within the disposal of God’s clock. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me? –Psalm 13:1.

Joseph patiently endured the ill treatment of his brothers and Potiphar, but the dungeon got long, and he entreated the butler to send for him when he was restored his position. But it was two full years (Genesis 41:1) until Pharoah dreamed and Joseph was finally hailed forth. But it was not so much the fault of the butler as it was the will of God who had called Joseph to be …laid in iron: Until the time that his word came: the word of the LORD tried him –Psalm 105:18-19. There is no more effective avenue to teach us patience than the discipline of darkness, from which few saints are exempt.

…Self-Pity

Yea, and certain women also of our company made us astonished, which were early at the sepulchre; And when they found not his body, they came, saying, that they had also seen a vision of angels, which said that he was alive –Luke 24:22-23. No one enjoys missing out. In fact, psychology has uncovered a new disorder –FOMO (fear of missing out). The tidings brought by the women was good news and an amazing turn of events, yet it brought the others no joy for it did not happen to them. Good news can rarely penetrate a person immersed in self-pity and Elijah was one such. His dark night arrived on the heels of a breathtaking triumph on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal. But in the blackness of his own inner feelings …he requested for himself that he might die; and said, It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers –1 Kings 19:4.

…Feelings of Failure

And certain of them which were with us went to the sepulchre, and found it even so as the women had said: but him they saw not –Luke 24:24. It is easy to think, “It worked for them but it’s not working for me.” While unsuccessful efforts may discourage us, it is not necessarily a failure on our part. John the Baptist had faithfully called the people to repentance, baptized Christ, and witnessed the thundering voice from heaven. He accurately announced the coming Messiah and pointed his disciples to …the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world –John 1:29. This ministry earned him a secure place in a dark prison cell. He had been well accustomed to the lack of comfort and a meager diet, but it was the feelings of utter abandonment by God that brought him unto dark doubts. And John calling unto him two of his disciples sent them to Jesus, saying, Art thou he that should come? or look we for another? –Luke 7:19.

“Was I wrong?” In the darkness he began to experience life on the sloping back of a question mark. John Bunyan describes it as the slough of despond. It may appear like D-Day for the Christian, but undue emphasis upon our unsuccessful efforts promotes no resurrection.

Conclusion

Not all spiritual darkness is completely avoidable. Not every spiritual experience is a time of heartfelt blessing, nor is every place. There are times of persecution and testing that are designed to bring saints unto the soul reckoning that only dark nights can minister unto. Jesus Himself was tempted in a similar manner to us, when in the pervading darkness of the ninth hour on the cross, His voice rang out …with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani? that is to say, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? –Matthew 27:46.

The road to Emmaus bears witness to the fact that a vibrant existence of faith gives no guarantee of the absence of spiritual depression. It is a story about real people with real faith experiencing real trials. It is helpful to teach us that even spiritual pleasures ought not to be held too tightly. Our confident visions for the future both immediate and long term must be immersed in the fires of humility. The dark night is the place where such self-deception dies, and an intimate knowledge of God is birthed. It transitions us from loving God for the blessings He gives us, to loving God for our relationship with Him and the communion that follows.

The traveling companion of Cleopas was never mentioned. Some think it was his wife. Some claim it was Luke. But their identity was omitted, perhaps so that we might be more apt to fill the vacancy with our own name. Seven miles from Jerusalem we stumble upon the stark reality of whom the Savior really is and that salvation is more than just a rubber stamp marking His possession. The scales fall from our eyes and the dark night of the soul gives way to the brightness of the noonday light of the presence of God. It is then that we make our joyous dash back to the city of peace only to be misunderstood again. And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them –Mark 16:13.

And so, I wonder even at the profitability of writing down such thoughts. It is not an encounter that can be manufactured and intellectually understood. It is a highly personal convocation with God and tailored specifically to each individual. But perhaps we, in our shallow generation, can be encouraged to reach out and embrace the darkness instead of meeting it with a loathing resistance. And there in the menacing darkness of night, learn to embrace the Savior of light.

Long my imprisoned spirit lay,
Fast bound in sin and nature's night.
Thine eye diffused a quickening ray,
I woke; the dungeon flamed with light.
My chains fell off. My heart was free.
I rose, went forth, and followed Thee.

- Charles Wesley

ואמר להם, אלו דברים אילו אתם מדברים זה עם זה בדרך, והייתם עצובים? –לוקס כד:יז.

ב־6 ביוני 1944, 156,000 חיילים אמריקאים, בריטים וקנדים נחתו על רצועת חוף של 50 מילים בנורמנדי שבצרפת. לאחר מספר חודשים של לחימה עזה, הם פרצו את ההגנות הראשוניות ופלשו לשטח שהיה בידי הגרמנים. המתקפה המפתיעה, הידועה כיום כיום D‑Day, תפסה את הגרמנים מופתעים. עם זאת, רק במרץ של השנה הבאה שוחררה צרפת לחלוטין מהכוחות הגרמניים. יום הפלישה היה התחלה של סוף מלחמת העולם השנייה בחזית המערבית, והאירוע שנראה כמי שמחליש את הצבא הגרמני המיוסר עד שלעולם לא התאושש. נדמה כמקרי שמילה רבות עם משמעות שלילית מתחילות באות D: Disappointment, Doubt, Doleful, Doom, Disillusionment, Discouragement, Dreary, Defeat, Despondency, Depression, Despair, Devastation, Deception, and Death.

אני יכול לדמיין ששני המאמינים האלה, שפוסעים בדרך לאמ אויאס באותו ערב עגום וחסר תקווה, הרגישו במקצת בדיוק באותו אופן. ה־D‑Day שלהם הגיע בלי שום התרעה. אני משער שכל אדם חי חווה מדי פעם רגעים של עצב עז — יום־D שלו, אם תרצו. אפילו בעלי חיים ידועים בהבעת דכדוך בהיעלמות אדונם או בן זוגם. אך נראה ששני התלמידים הללו חוו כאב שמעבר לאובדן רגיל של חבר. הם הביטו אל פנים המציאות המדכאת שכל תקוותיהם המתוקות למחר זוהר נמחצו לערימה הרוסה לרגלי הצלב.

הייסורים הללו לא היו התקף דיכאון רגיל אלא דיכאון שקשור למשבר אמונה. סוג זה של ייאוש רוחני הוא מצב של צער רוחני עמוק שבו המאמין הנאבק והנואש מרגיש שהושאר בידי אלוהים. זו תחושת יאוש שהשמש של ברכת האלוהים הוסתרה והלילה האפל של הנשמה הפך לדייר קבע בתוכה.

בעוד כולנו שואפים להתנגד באומץ לפיתויים כה חשוכים, חיפוש קצר בחייהם של אנשי אלוהים רבים יראה כי פיתויים אלה אמיתיים ונפוצים בבני אדם. במצב כזה, החיים נראים בלתי אפשריים והעצב המשקע בלב אינו רואה אור בקצה המנהרה. מדוע כאבי תמידי ולשוני רפאו לא: מה ניצלני? האם תתפס כלפי שקר אלי, ומים הנגאים? –ירמיהו טו:יח. זו כמובן הגזמה דרמטית שיצאה מפיו של הנביא הבוכה, אך היא נותנת לנו מבט ישיר אל הכאב הנורא בעומק נשמתו.

ולא נרצה, אחי, שתהיו בלא דעת על הצרה אשר קרתה לנו באסיה, כי הועמדנו על גבול היותנו מעבר לכוח, עד שנואשנו אף מן החיים; כי שמנו בתוכנו את משפט המוות, למען לא נתפלל על עצמנו, כי אם על האל אשר מקים מתים –קורינתים ב׳ א:ח-ט. הלילה האפל של הנשמה אינו מבחין בין אנשים. הוא פולש לחייהם של נסיכים ועניים, מטיפים ותשובים, ציבוריים ופרטיים, בבמות וכסאות. שני התלמידים הללו עברו שוב ושוב בעל־פה על כל התרחישים האפשריים בדרכם בדרך אמואים. אין ספק שמצאו המון פגמים באחרים וגם חרטה אישית. ה״מה־לולי״ ו״אם־רק״ נדונו לעומק, אך כלום לא יכול היה לשנות את התוצאה והחרדה חסרת השקט נותרה.

הדרך מירושלים לאמואס הייתה כארבעים ושמונה פרלאס או ככאן שבע מילין. ובמהלך המסע העצוב הזה הצטרף זר אל השניים הנבוכים ביום־D שלהם וביקש מהם דין וחשבון על עצבותם. אך הוא איננו צופה סקרן. הוא האדון המכונה, שקם כדי לשפוך את אורו השמימי על הדרך המחשיכה שלנו. במקום לגלות את עצמו בפתאומיות, ואולי לטובתם, הוא בסבלנות מאפשר להם לחשוף את הדרך הרוחנית החרבה שעליה פסעו.

כך השיחה נפתחת ככל שעוברות קטעי הדרך, כל אחד מגלה את מאמצינו השגויים הכנים שמרחיקים אותנו מעיר השלום ואל תוך הלילה האפל של הנשמה…

…הבערות של אחרים

ואחד מהם, אשר שמו היה קלופא, ענה לו ויאמר, האם אתה נודד בירושלים וכל לא ידעת את הדברים האשר קרו בימים האלה שם? –לוקס כד:יח. שאלו כל זר ברחובות ניו‑יורק מדוע הדגלים הורדו לחצי התורן שלושה ימים אחרי נפילת המגדלים ב־11 בספטמבר, ותקבלו את אותה תשובה תמוהה שיוחסה לשניים האלה. ״איך אתה כל כך בור?״ כולנו נוטים לתהות על אנשים שאינם חולקים את הידע שאנו מדמיינים כי לנו יש. ככל שאדם צעיר יותר, כך יותר תשובות שהוא בטוח שמאגר הידיעה שלו מכיל.

זה לא חדש. משה, בעודו צעיר, …חשב שאחיו יבינו כי על ידם יפדווהו אלה, אך לא ידעו –מעשי השליחים ז׳:כה. בעודו בטוח כי הוא מחזיק בתוכנית האל, הוא טעה בחישוב המידה שנמצא בידו. אם המעשה שלנו לא יכול לתקן את המצב הנתון, התשובות שלנו אינן התשובות האמיתיות. השנאה הלבבית שנוצרת כלפי אלה שמבינים אחרת היא סימן ראשון לכך שאנו בדרך שגויה. כשהלך לו מרחק רב בדרך החיים, משה החל להרגיש את ייאוש הכאב ואת חשכת השעה. ואיני יכול לישא לבדי את העם הזה, כי כבד ממני מזה; ואם תעשה זאת לי, הוצאני נא מיד, אם מצאתי חן בעיניך, ואל־אראה עוד את רעתי –במדבר יא:יד-טו. מדוע משה לא ראה זאת קודם? מאותו סיבה שעיניהם של התלמידים האלה …נרגעו שלא יכירוהו –לוקס כד:טז.

…השכל

ויאמר להם, אילו דברים? ויאמרו אליו, על ישוע הנצרי אשר היה נביא גבור במעשה ובמלה לפני האל וכל העם –לוקס כד:יט. הם שמרו לעצמם תפיסה פרטית מי היה המשיח, אך ראו הם …באין־שקף, בקושי… –קורינתים א׳ יג:יב. ידיעתם החלקית נשענה חזק על הבנתם שלהם וחיפשה את סוג הגאולה המוטעה. בעיניהם, המושיע שלהם היה (בעבר) נביא שלא יוכל עוד לעשות את אשר רצו שיעשה. כולנו רוצייים שיהיה ישוע פותר את בעיותינו ומרפא רגשותינו, אבל מטרתו היא לשחררנו מתפיסתנו ומחטאנו.

ליעקב הייתה כל סיבה להאמין שזכות הבכורה והברכה היו לו. בבית‑אל, אלוהים הבטיח לברכו. יעקב חשב שזה יגיע בצורה חומרית. ויץ יעקב נדר, אם־יהי ה' עמדי ושמרני בדרך הזאת אשר אנכי הולך, ויתן־לי לחם לאכל ובגד לאל־לבש, ואשר אשוב בשלום אל־בית אבי, יהיה ה' לי לאל –בראשית כח:כ-כא.

אך הברכה הגדולה ביותר שקיבל מאלוהים הגיעה כנף לילה אפל ועמוק. ויצרב יעקב לבדו; ויעמד איש אתו וילחם אתו עד־שחר. וירא כי לא יוכל עמו ויגע במפשעתו, ותצא כף יעקב ממקומה בהתחשב כחושב אותו. ויאמר, שחר; ישלחני מאץ. ויאמר, לא אשילך עד־ברכתני. ויאמר לו, מה־שמך? ויאמר, יעקב. ויאמר, לא־יקרא עוד שמך יעקב כי אם־ישרא; כי במקום מי שקרא נסיך תהיה ידך על־כוח אלהים ועל־אנשים ותמצנע –בראשית לב:כד-כח.

יעקב כבר צבר שפע נכסים ארציים. מה עוד יכול היה לרצות? הלילה היה אפל ליעקב כשגילה שבלהיברו את חייו רדף אחר רכוש והתנגד לאלוהים. עתה הוא מבקש אופי נשגב ושפע רוחני. ניצחונו היה דרך הכנעה, והוא צעד כצולע עם כתר. ה' אינו יכול לברך אדם במלואו עד שכבש תחילה את כוחות השכל שלו.

…גורל רע

ואיך נשיאי הכהנים ומנהיגינו מסרו אותו להווגד למוות, וצלבו אותו –לוקס כד:כ. אלוהים מתמחה בהפיכת דילמות כבדות לנצחונות עצומים. עדיין, האדם מסתכל סביבו וקונס על החשכה שסביבו. אף על פי שיכולה להיות תגובת חסד מצדו, …הבקר בעיניהם כמט ממשלת־מיתה… –איוב כד:יז. להדגיש יתר על המידה את הרע שבנו הוא לעג לדרת האלוהות. למרות שכולנו עלולים להתחרט לפעמים על דברים שהיינו יכולים לעשות או לומר אחרת, עלינו להשאיר את התוצאות בידי האלוהים. איוב חווה מי יידע גורל רע כמוהו. עד כדי כך שפתח …את פיו, וקלל את יומו. ויאמר איוב, יכחד יום הולדתי, ולילה שבו נאמר, הובן ילד; יהי היום ההוא חשכה; אל יתחנן עליו אלוהים מלמעלה ואל־זרח האור עליו. יהי חשך וצל־מוות נתן עליו; ורוח תגור עליו; יהי חשכת היום מפחידה אותו. וכשם־הלילה־ההוא, יהי עליו חשך… –איוב ג:א-ו. אך במקום כלשהו לפני שהמאורעות האפלים תוקנו והרימו, האור האיר בנפשו, והוא שם ידו על פיו והשתחווה.

…אג׳נדה אישית

ואנחנו קיווינו כי הוא הוא אשר יגאל את ישראל… –לוקס כד:כא. טבעי לנסות להבין מצב נתון ושניים אלה בחרו את המשוואה הנכונה. טפשותם הייתה בהנחה על אמצעי הגאולה שיספק המשיח וסוג הגאולה שיקבלו. הם ציפו ליום שבו עמם יוערך על־ידי הרומאים. כאשר אנו מחפשים ללא דעת את ביטחוננו האישי, זה מוביל בוודאי לאכזבה מרה. נעמן חשב …יצא אלי, ויעמד וישא שם את־שמו של ה' אלוהיו ויביא ידו על המקום ויתקן את מצורעתו –מלכים ב׳ ה:יא.

אברהם הובטח בארץ כנען וביקש אישור. הוא הכין את קורבן הברית שהורה לו אלוהים, אך כל היום עבר ואלוהים לא עשה עמם דבר. ובשקיעת השמש נפל על־אברם שינה עמוקה, והנה אימת חשך גדול נפלה עליו –בראשית טו:יב.

כאשר אברהם חיכה לאלוהים לקבל את מנחתו, המשיך לדחוק את עופות הטרף. אך כשקרב הערב החל להרגיש שנעזב מאת ה' ולאט־לאט נפל הלילה השחור על נשמתו. צריך חוויה של חצות כדי שהדברים יהיו אפלים מספיק שנוכל לראות את הכוכבים ושקט מספיק כדי לשמוע את קולו. והיינו נשמים במשפט המוות בתוכנו למען לא נשען על עצמנו, כי אם על האל המקים מתים –קורינתים ב׳ א:ט.

…חוסר סבלנות

…ובנוסף על־כל זאת, היום הוא היום השלישי מאז הדברים האלה נעשו –לוקס כד:כא. רבים מאתנו מספיק ממושמעים כדי להחזיק מעמד לעונה. כשתקוותנו נדחית (ראו משלי יג:יב), ליבנו נעשה חולה ונדכא. שלושה ימים נראו לאלה כזמן ארוך. אך שלושה ימים, שבועות, חודשים, שנים או אפילו עשורים הם כולם בתחום שעון האלוהים. עד־מתי תשכחני, ה' לנצח? עד־מתי תסתיר פני ממני? –תהלים יג:א.

יוסף ניחם בסבלנות את העוול מאחיו ואת תקופת פוטיפר, אך הבור התמשך והוא ביקש מן־הכסאי שישלח לו כשישוחזר מעמדו. אך עברו שנתיים שלמות (בראשית מ:א) עד שפרעה חלם ויוסף הובא בסופו של דבר. אך זאת לא הייתה כל כך אשמת הכסאי כמו רצון האל שקרא ליוסף להיות …שמוׁשולף בברזל: עד־עת דברו בא: דבר־יהוה נסה אותו –תהלים קה:יח-יט. אין דרך יעילה יותר ללמדם סבלנות מאשר משמעת החשכה, שמעטים מהקדושים פטורים ממנה.

…חמלה עצמית

אף נשים מן חברתנו הלכו ונדהמו, שהיו מוקדם בקבר; וכאשר לא מצאו את־גופו, באו ודברו, כי ראו חזיון של מלאכים, שאמרו שהוא חי –לוקס כד:כב-כג. איש לא מחבב להחמיץ. למעשה, הפסיכולוגיה גילתה הפרעה חדשה — FOMO (הפחד להחמיץ). הבשורה שהביאו הנשים היתה דבר מבשר ואירוע מדהים, ובכל זאת היא לא נתנה שמחה לאחרים כי לא קרה להם. בשורות טובות קשה לחדור לאדם שקוע בחמלה עצמית, ואליהו היה כזה. הלילה האפל שלו הגיע בעקבות ניצחון נהדר על הר עם הבעלים נגד נביאי בעל. אך בתוך השחור של רגשותיו הוא …התפלל שימות; ויאמר, מספיק זה; ה' קח־נא את־נפשי כי אינני טוב מבני־אבותי –מלכים א׳ יט:ד.

…תחושות של כישלון

ואחרים מן אשר היו עמנו הלכו אל־הקבר, ומצאו כן כשאמרו הנשים; אבל לא ראוהו –לוקס כד:כד. קל לחשוב ״זה עבד להם אבל לא לי״. בעוד שמאמצים כושלים עלולים לייאש אותנו, זה לאו דווקא כישלון מצידנו. יוחנן המטביל קרא בעקביות לעם תשובה, טבל את המשיח, ושמע קול רועם מן השמיים. הוא הכריז במדויק על בוא המשיח והצביע לתלמידיו על …שהשיל את חטאת העולם –יוחנן א׳ א:כב. שירות זה הביא אותו למקום בטוח בתא כלא חשוך. הוא התרגל לחוסר נוחות ותזונה דלה, אך תחושות ההשארה המוחלטת בידי אלוהים היו שהביאוהו לספקות אפלים. ויקרא יוחנן אל־שניהם מתלמידיו וישלחם אל ישוע לאמר, אתה הוא הבא, או נמתין אנו לאחר? –לוקס ז:יט.

״טעיתי?״ בחושך החל לחוות את החיים על גב שיפוע של סימן שאלה. ג'ון בניון מתאר זאת כשפת הבי־נח. זה עשוי להיראות כמו D‑Day לנוצרי, אך הדגשה מופרזת על מאמצינו הכושלים לא מקדמת שום תחיית רוח.

מסקנה

לא כל חשכה רוחנית ניתנת למניעה מלאה. לא כל חוויה רוחנית היא זמן של ברכה לבבית, וגם לא כל מקום. יש זמנים של רדיפות וניסיונות שמטרתם להוביל את הקדושים אל רישום הנשמה שרק הלילות האפלים יכולים לשרת. ישוע עצמו נתנסה באופן דומה לנו, כאשר בשעת החשכה העמוקה של השעה התשיעית על הצלב, קראה קולו …בקול גדול ויאמר, אלי, אלי, למה שבקתני? כלומר, אלהי, אלהי, למה עזבתני? –מתתיהו כז:מד.

הדרך לאמואס מעידה כי קיום אמונה תוססת אינו מבטיח היעדר דיכאון רוחני. זאת סיפור על אנשים אמיתיים עם אמונה אמתית שחווים נסיונות אמיתיים. זה עוזר ללמד אותנו שגם עינוגים רוחניים לא ראוי לאחוז בהם חזק מדי. חזיונותינו הבטוחים לעתיד, גם המיידיים וגם הרחוקים, חייבים להיות מוטבלים באש הענווה. הלילה האפל הוא המקום שבו הטעות העצמית מגיעה למותה, ומולדת בו ידיעה אינטימית של אלוהים. הוא מעביר אותנו מאהבת אלוהים בעקבות הברכות שהוא נותן, לאהבת אלוהים בעבור יחסינו עמו ובשיתוף הנלווה.

חבר הנסיעה של קלופא מעולם לא הוזכר בשמו. יש הסבורים שזה אשתו. אחרים טוענים שזה לוק. אך זהותו הושמטה, אולי כדי שנגיש למלא את הריק בשם שלנו. שבע מילין מירושלים נתקלנו במציאות הנוקבת מי המש Savior באמת וכי הישועה היא יותר מסתם חותמת גומי שמסמנת בעלותו. הרקיעים נפלו מעינינו ולילה־נשמה אפל נתן מקום לאור הצהרים הנוכחות האלוהית. אז רצנו בשמחה בחזרה אל עיר השלום ורק שונינו לא הבינו אותנו שוב. וילכו ויספרו לשאר; ולא האמינו להם –מארק טז:יג.

ולכן, אני תוהה אף על־תועלת כיצירת מחשבות מסוג זה בכתב. זוהי לא מפגש שניתן לייצר ולהבין שכלית. זה כינוס אישי מאוד עם האל ומתאים במיוחד לכל פרט ופרט. אבל אולי אנו, בדור הרדוד שלנו, יכולים לעודד להגיע החוצה ולחבק את החשכה במקום לפגוש אותה בשנאה ובדחייה. ושם, בחשכת הלילה המאיימת, ללמוד לחבק את מושיע האור.

ארוכות נשמותי היינו כלואות,
כבולות בחטא ולילה של טבעי.
עיניך הזרימו קרן מחיה,
התעוררתי; הבור נפל אור בוהק.
אזרחותי נשרו. לבי שוחרר.
קמתי, יצאתי והלכתי בעקבותיך.

- צ'ארלס וזוילי

It’s been said that in the 1500s, after baptism, the Anabaptists lived an average of only 27 days. They were hunted and killed. They realized one thing—serving Christ would most certainly cost them everything. They forsook the comforts of easy living; they forsook it all. It could also have been a similar situation when Jesus walked on the earth, or shortly after He was killed.

…and he turned, and said unto them, If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple. For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish. Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple –Luke 14:25-33.

Jesus clearly asked His disciples to count the cost. And they must have counted the cost, for they faithfully gave all, including their lives, for Christ’s Kingdom. They realized they could have had the good things in this life; however, they also realized it would cost them the good things in the next.

Yea, and all that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution –2 Timothy 3:12. If we look at the promises which Jesus gave us in His Word about persecution, and then compare them with the lives of Jesus’ followers today, we might be confused. And rightfully so.

He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked –1 John 2:6. Jesus says we should walk as He walked, He also tells us that we need to follow Him.

How did He walk? We know that Jesus had no place to lay His head—this was how He wanted it. We know that Jesus could have chosen to live where and how He wanted. He was, in fact, in control of the whole world, yet He was despised and rejected by the world and its system. When He spoke, people wanted to lay their hands on Him; they wanted to kill Him. He was not a popular person; He had few friends. In reality, He didn’t fit in, and He didn’t last long. Three years after His ministry began, He was killed. …He was numbered with the transgressors –Mark 15:28.

What about His followers today? Are they walking how He walked? And if not, why not?

We read about the children of Israel going through the wilderness. They fought and overtook the cities in their paths, killing all in the process. We read many accounts about how God instructed the children of Israel to kill all of the enemy, even the women and children. The following is one such account of many.

So the LORD our God delivered into our hands Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people: and we smote him until none was left to him remaining. And we took all his cities at that time, there was not a city which we took not from them, threescore cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All these cities were fenced with high walls, gates, and bars; beside unwalled towns a great many. And we utterly destroyed them, as we did unto Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying the men, women, and children, of every city –Deuteronomy 3:3-6.

We read accounts like this in scripture, and it can cause us to cringe. It is almost as if life itself was not important. Even in the New Testament, death doesn’t seem to be that big of a deal. People lived and people died.

The first week after we moved to Haiti, I was driving through the city. Suddenly, right in front of me I saw a man lying in the street. Blood ran down the road and pooled in a low spot—he was dead. I was shocked. But what shocked me the most was that no one seemed to notice. People by the hundreds busily walked around him, not even looking at the man—no one cared.

Over the next six years we saw many dead or dying people—it became a normal scene.

If that was how it was back in the Bible times, and it is still how it is today in many countries of the world, maybe we are the ones that are out of the norm? Maybe we esteem life higher than God does. Maybe we are among those that Jesus spoke of when He said—He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal –John 12:25.

In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return –Genesis 3:19. We were created out of the dust, and after a few short years, we return to the very same dust.

Whereas ye know not what shall be on the morrow. For what is your life? It is even a vapour, that appeareth for a little time, and then vanisheth away –James 4:14. The Bible also calls our lives a vapor.

We all know what happens after that—the judgment, then eternity. So why do we care so much about this life? Maybe it is an American problem or a western problem.

It is obvious that Americans are looked upon as ‘more valuable’ than most other nationalities. If you are an American in a developing country, you are heralded as a king. If something happens to an American, it is quickly headline news. I once stood over the bodies of two murdered men. One of their close friends stood by, so I asked him how he was doing. He shrugged and said, “This is life”.

So why does life mean so much to us Americans? The answer is simple. We can obtain almost anything we want; money is easy to get, and we can live how we want. We can live in pleasure every day. We go to the store and buy what we want, when we want—we have it our way. This is just how it is; for most of us it is all we have ever known—the life of plenty. So how does this affect us?

This type of living makes it especially hard to ‘give all’ for Christ. It makes it difficult to obey Jesus’ command to …Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature –Mark 16:15. It makes it difficult to say with the Apostle Paul, For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain –Philippians 1:21. In reality, it makes it difficult to be a Christian.

When Jesus said… For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it –Matthew 16:25, what did He mean? Could it mean literally just what it says: that when you fall in love with your own life, you cannot effectively follow Christ, so that in the end you will actually lose your life?

Can you go to the lost and forsake the comforts of this life if it’s those comforts that you love and live for? It’s not likely. What we have is “Americanized” Christians that will only go to the mission field if they can take their comforts with them. This produces rich, comfortable missionaries who, despite their best efforts, can’t win the lost, rather they make them jealous. Can we go into the cities and preach the gospel to the lost like so many before us have? Can we take time to teach and disciple the tens of thousands who are seeking? If we love our lives, we probably will not, since there is too much to lose and it’s a waste of good talent and opportunity. God help us.

When we are living to please the flesh and we have our lives figured out, it is hard for God to use us. We are puffed up. We tend to believe that God has blessed us because of all our possessions and our status in life; but isn’t this the prosperity gospel? What if that changed? Would we still consider ourselves to be blessed? Is it God or our own doing that causes us to be joyful? What if we found ourselves in John the Baptist’s shoes? Or the Apostle Paul’s? If we would be sitting in prison for doing nothing wrong, would our joy remain? It should if the Holy Spirit is living and working in our hearts. The Bible says that we can suffer joyfully!

Years ago, a coworker of mine was a happy fellow. He had a nice life. There was one problem—he did not believe there was a God. We would talk day after day. He would constantly tell me how happy he was and that one didn’t need to be a Christian to be happy. He would talk about his nice life, all that he possessed, his good job, his nice family. Interestingly enough, he truly did seem happy.

I would tell him that true happiness didn’t come from the things that we possess or the position that we find ourselves in, but he would just disagree. He also proclaimed that he lived a better life than most Christians that he knew. He also said he didn’t get angry like most Christians and could control himself. I tried to convince him that he was deceived. At times I would think I was getting somewhere with him, then later it would seem I was far from reaching him. One day he soberly admitted that I seemed to be different that most Christians he had known in the past, but that still wasn’t enough.

I left that job and lost contact with him. Recently, I ran into another one of my former coworkers. I quickly thought of my friend and asked how he was doing. He looked at me strangely and then shocked me to my core as he said, “He committed suicide”.

The devil wants us to love our life—it’s that simple. When we love our life, we focus on it, we cherish it. The last thing we want to do is lose our life, even if it is for something eternal.

When I was in the Marines, they would constantly remind us that our lives were not number one; our country was. There are many young men who put their country first. Many have gone and given their all; many have died.

In World War 2, the Japanese would try to sneak up to a fox hole housing soldiers and throw in a grenade. Many times, it didn’t end like the Japanese wanted, because someone would jump on the grenade, absorbing the explosion. Thousands gave their lives to save their friends and defend their country. But be sure, if their priorities were not in order (of country first before themselves), they would not have done so.

If someone today, in America, would risk their life for the sake of the gospel, he would be labeled as foolish, reckless, and immature. But what do we say about so many before us—the ones that gave their lives while standing for the same things that we say we believe today? And what about the thousands today who are putting their lives on the line in other countries—are they foolish? Let’s look at a very obvious example in Acts.

And as we tarried there many days, there came down from Judaea a certain prophet, named Agabus. And when he was come unto us, he took Paul’s girdle, and bound his own hands and feet, and said, Thus saith the Holy Ghost, So shall the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man that owneth this girdle, and shall deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles. And when we heard these things, both we, and they of that place, besought him not to go up to Jerusalem. Then Paul answered, What mean ye to weep and to break mine heart? for I am ready not to be bound only, but also to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus. –Acts 21:10-13.

What would we think of Paul’s actions today? Paul went to Jerusalem and was quickly taken, beaten, and put in prison. It was the beginning of the end for our dear brother. He was moved from prison to prison and eventually ended up in Rome where he was beheaded. What do you think the ones that tried to persuade him to not go to Jerusalem thought? Do you think they called him a fool? Did they shake their heads and say, “I told him not to go!”?

We cannot know for sure. However, I am sure that Paul was simply putting the kingdom of Christ first; his life did not matter. He was obeying God, and God had told him to go.

When we love our lives, it is very difficult to be an effective disciple of the Lord Jesus. We end up forsaking God’s calling and then we are stuck trying to live the Christian life alone, and without God—no spiritual help from above, causing us to fall way short of the mark.

It’s ironic that only when we forsake all, including our lives, will we find true peace and purpose for our lives. And when we love our lives, that is when we will lose them.

Rise up, O saints of God!
Have done with lesser things.
Give heart and soul and mind and strength
To serve the King of kings.

Rise up, O saints of God!
The kingdom tarries long.
Bring in the day of Christlike love
And end the night of wrong.

Lift high the cross of Christ!
Tread where His feet have trod.
Led onward by the Son of Man,
Rise up, O saints of God!

Let us rise up, as God’s people, and begin to be done with lesser things, with our gaze on things above, not on the things of this earth. Yes, we will stand out; we will be labeled fools and many other things. However, we will once again catch God’s attention and the fires of revival will once again burn!

قيل إن في القرن الخامس عشر، بعد المعمودية، كان الأناخبتيون يعيشون في المتوسط لمدة 27 يومًا فقط. كانوا مطاردين ويُقتَلون. أدركوا شيئًا واحدًا—خدمة المسيح ستكون بالتأكيد مكلفة لهم بكل شيء. تركوا ملذات الحياة السهلة؛ تركوها كلها. وقد تكون الحالة مشابهة أيضًا عندما سار يسوع على الأرض، أو بعد موته بقليل.

…فتَحَوَّل وقال لهم: إن جاء أحد إليَّ ولم يَكْرَهْ أباه وأمه وزوجته وأولاده وإخوته وأخواته، بل ونفسه أيضاً، لا يقدر أن يكون تلميذي. ومن لا يحمل صليبه ويتبعني، لا يقدر أن يكون تلميذي. أيُّكم إذن، يريد أن يبني برجًا، أما يجلس أولًا ويحسب النفقات، أي هل له ما يكفي لإتمامه؟ لئلاّ إذا وضع الأساس ولم يستطِع أن يتمم، بدأ كل الناظرين يسخرون منه، قائلين: هذا الذي ابتدأ يبني ولم يقدر أن يتمم. أو أي ملك ذاكرًا أن يذهب إلى حرب مع ملك آخر، أما يجلس أولًا ويبتدر المشورة هل يقدر بعشرة آلاف أن يلاقي من يأتي عليه بعشرين ألفًا؟ وإلاّ وهو بعد بعيدًا جدًا، يرسل سفراء ويطلب شروط السلام. كذلك من لا يترك كل ما له لا يقدر أن يكون تلميذي—لوقا 14:25-33.

بوضوح طلب يسوع من تلاميذه أن يحسبوا الثمن. ولا بد أنهم حسبوا الثمن، لأنهم بذلوا كل شيء بأمانة، بما في ذلك حياتهم، من أجل ملكوت المسيح. أدركوا أنهم كان بإمكانهم أن ينالوا الخيرات في هذه الحياة؛ ومع ذلك أدركوا أيضًا أنه سيكلفهم الخيرات في الحياة الآتية.

نعم، وكل الذين يريدون أن يعيشوا تقوياً في المسيح يسوع يتعرضون للاضطهاد –2 تيموثاوس 3:12. إذا نظرنا إلى الوعود التي أعطاها يسوع لنا في كلمته عن الاضطهاد، ثم قارناها بحياة أتباع يسوع اليوم، فقد نَحتار. وعن حق.

من يقُل إنه يقيم فيه، ينبغي أن يسلك هو أيضًا كما سلك—1 يوحنا 2:6. يقول يسوع إنه ينبغي أن نسلك كما سلك، ويخبرنا أيضًا أننا بحاجة إلى أن نتبعه.

كيف سلك؟ نعلم أن يسوع لم يكن له موضع ليضع رأسه—هكذا أرادها. نعلم أن يسوع كان يستطيع أن يختار أين وكيف يعيش. فقد كان، في الواقع، مسيطرًا على العالم كله، ومع ذلك كان مزدرًى ومرفوضًا من العالم ونظامه. عندما تكلم، أراد الناس أن يضعوا أيديهم عليه؛ أرادوا أن يقتلوه. لم يكن شخصًا محبوبًا؛ كان له أصدقاء قليلون. في الحقيقة، لم يندمج ولم يدم طويلاً. بعد ثلاث سنوات من بدء خدمته، قُتل. …وزوِّج مع المجرمين—مرقس 15:28.

ماذا عن أتباعه اليوم؟ هل يسلكون كما سلك؟ وإن لم يفعلوا، فلماذا لا؟

نقرأ عن بني إسرائيل وهم يعبرون البرية. كانوا يقاتلون ويغلبون المدن في طريقهم، ويقتلون جميع من فيها. نقرأ العديد من الحوادث التي كان الله يوجّه فيها بني إسرائيل لقتل كل العدو، حتى النساء والأطفال. فيما يلي أحد هذه الروايات العديدة.

فأسلم الرب إلهنا في أيدينا أيضًا أوج ملك باشان وكل شعبه، فهزمناه حتى لم يبقَ له شيء. وأخذنا جميع مُدنه في ذلك الوقت، لم تكن مدينة لم نأخذها منهم، ستون مدينة كلها إقليم أرجوب، مملكة أوج في باشان. وكل هذه المدن كانت محصّنة بأسوار عالية وبأبواب وعتاد؛ إلى جانب قرى كثيرة غير مسورة. فأهلكناهم أهلاكًا تامًا، كما فعلنا بسِهْرون ملك حِشبون، أهلاكًا تامًا الرجال والنساء والأطفال من كل مدينة—تثنية 3:3-6.

نقرأ حوادث كهذه في الكتاب المقدس، وقد تجعلنا نتجافى. يكاد يبدو كما لو أن الحياة نفسها لم تكن مهمة. حتى في العهد الجديد، لا يبدو أن الموت أمرٌ جللٌ إلى هذا الحد. الناس عاشوا وماتوا.

في الأسبوع الأول بعد انتقالنا إلى هايتي، كنت أقود السيارة عبر المدينة. فجأة، رأيت أمامي رجلًا مستلقيًا في الشارع. سال الدم أسفل الطريق وتجمع في مكان منخفض—كان قد مات. صدمت. لكن ما صَدَمَني أكثر هو أن لا أحد بدا وكأنه يلاحظ. مئات الناس كانوا يمشون حوله بنشاط، دون أن ينظروا حتى إلى الرجل—لا أحد اهتم.

خلال الست سنوات التالية رأينا كثيرين ميتين أو ميئوسين—أصبح مشهدًا عاديًا.

إذا كان هذا حالَ الأزمنة الكتابية، ولا يزال كذلك اليوم في كثير من دول العالم، فربما نحن من خرج عن المألوف؟ ربما نعظّم الحياة أكثر مما يفعل الله. ربما نحن من الذين تكلم عنهم يسوع عندما قال—من يحب حياته يهلكها، ومن يبغض حياته في هذا العالم يحفظها للحياة الأبدية—يوحنا 12:25.

بعرق وجهك تأكل خبزًا حتى ترجع إلى الأرض، لأنها منها أخذت؛ لأنك تراب وإلى تراب ترجع—تكوين 3:19. خُلقنا من التراب، وبعد سنوات قليلة نعود إلى نفس التراب.

أنتم لا تعلمون ماذا يكون غدًا. لأن ما هي حياتكم؟ إنها بخار يظهر قليلاً ثم يزول—يعقوب 4:14. يَسمي الكتاب حياتنا أيضًا بخارًا.

كلنا نعلم ما يحدث بعد ذلك—الحكم، ثم الأبدية. فلماذا نهتم كثيرًا بهذه الحياة؟ ربما هي مشكلة أمريكية أو غربية.

من الواضح أن الأمريكيين يُنظر إليهم على أنهم «أثمن» من معظم الجنسيات الأخرى. إذا كنت أمريكيًا في بلد نامٍ، فأنت تُستقبَل كالملك. إذا حدث شيء لأمريكي، يُصبح خبرًا عاجلًا. وقفت مرة فوق جثتي رجلين قتُلا. كان أحد أصدقائهما المقربين واقفًا بجانبهما، فسألته كيف حاله. هز كتفيه وقال: «هذه هي الحياة».

فلماذا تعني الحياة كثيرًا لنا نحن الأمريكيين؟ الجواب بسيط. يمكننا الحصول على أي شيء نريد تقريبًا؛ المال سهل المنال، ويمكننا العيش كما نشاء. يمكننا أن نعيش بالملذات كل يوم. نذهب إلى المتجر ونشتري ما نريد، متى نريد—نحصل على ما نريده بطريقتنا. هذا هو الواقع؛ بالنسبة لمعظمنا، هذا كل ما عرفناه على الإطلاق—حياة الزيادة. فكيف يؤثر ذلك علينا؟

هذا النوع من العيش يجعل من الصعب بشكل خاص «أن تعطي كل شيء» للمسيح. يجعل من الصعب طاعة أمر يسوع أن …اذهبوا إلى جميع الخليقة وابلغوا الإنجيل—مرقس 16:15. يجعل من الصعب أن نقول مع الرسول بولس، لأني إن عشت فالمسيح لي، وإن مت فربح—فيلبي 1:21. في الواقع، يجعل من الصعب أن تكون مسيحيًا.

عندما قال يسوع… فمن أراد أن يخلّص نفسه يهلكها، ومن أهلك نفسه من أجلي يجدها—متى 16:25، ماذا عنى؟ هل يمكن أن يعني حرفيًا ما يقوله: أنه عندما تقع في حب حياتك لا تستطيع أن تتبع المسيح بفعالية، بحيث أنك في النهاية ستفقد حياتك بالفعل؟

هل يمكنك أن تذهب إلى الضالين وتترك ملذات هذه الحياة إذا كانت تلك الملذات هي ما تحبه وتعيش لأجله؟ من غير المحتمل. ما لدينا الآن هو مسيحيون «أمركنوا» لا يذهبون إلى الحقل التبشيري إلا إذا استطاعوا أن يأخذوا ملذاتهم معهم. هذا ينتج مبشرين أثرياء ومترفّين الذين، على الرغم من جهودهم الطيبة، لا يستطيعون كسب الضالين، بل يجعلونهم يغارون. هل نستطيع أن ندخل المدن ونبشر الإنجيل للضالين كما فعل كثيرون قبلنا؟ هل نأخذ الوقت لتعليم وتلمذة عشرات الآلاف الذين يطلبون؟ إذا أحببنا حياتنا، فربما لا نفعل، لأن هناك الكثير لنخسره ومن الخسارة إهدار للمواهب والفرص الجيدة. ليعيننا الله.

حين نعيش لإرضاء الجسد ولدينا حياتنا منظمة، يصعب على الله أن يستخدمنا. نصبح متعظمين. نميل إلى الاعتقاد أن الله باركنا بسبب كل ممتلكاتنا ومركزنا في الحياة؛ لكن أليس هذا إنجيل الازدهار؟ ماذا لو تغيّر ذلك؟ هل سنزال نعتبر أنفسنا مباركين؟ هل هو الله أم فعلنا نحن الذي يجعلنا فرحين؟ ماذا لو وجدنا أنفسنا في موضع يوحنا المعمدان؟ أو موضع الرسول بولس؟ إن كنا سنجلس في السجن ظلمًا، هل ستبقى فرحتنا؟ ينبغي أن تبقى إذا كان الروح القدس ساكنًا ويعمل في قلوبنا. الكتاب يقول إننا نستطيع أن نتألم بفرح!

منذ سنوات، كان أحد زملائي في العمل إنسانًا سعيدًا. كان له حياة طيبة. كان هناك مشكلة واحدة—لم يؤمن بوجود إله. كنا نتحدث يومًا بعد يوم. كان يقول لي باستمرار كم هو سعيد وأنه لا يحتاج أن يكون مسيحيًا ليكون سعيدًا. كان يتحدث عن حياته الطيبة، وكل ما يملك، ووظيفته الجيدة، وعائلته الطيبة. ومن الغريب، بدا حقًا سعيدًا.

قلت له إن السعادة الحقيقية لا تأتي من الأشياء التي نمتلكها ولا من المكانة التي نجد أنفسنا فيها، لكنه كان يختلف معي. وأعلن أيضًا أنه يعيش حياة أفضل من معظم المسيحيين الذين عرفهم. وقال أيضًا إنه لا يغضب كما يغضب معظم المسيحيين ويمكنه أن يتحكم في نفسه. حاولت أن أقنعه أنه مضلّل. أحيانًا كنت أظن أنني أقطع شوطًا معه، ثم يبدو لاحقًا أنني بعيد جدًا عن الوصول إليه. في يوم ما اعترف بجديّة أنني أبدو مختلفًا عن معظم المسيحيين الذين عرفهم في الماضي، لكن ذلك لم يكن كافيًا.

تركت تلك الوظيفة وفقدت الاتصال به. مؤخرًا، التقيت بأحد زملائي السابقين في العمل. تذكرت صديقي سريعًا وسألت كيف حاله. نظر إليّ بغرابة ثم صدمني حتى أعماق روحي عندما قال: «انتحر».

الشيطان يريد منا أن نحب حياتنا—الأمر بهذه البساطة. عندما نحب حياتنا، نركّز عليها، ونقدّرها. آخر ما نريد فعله هو أن نفقد حياتنا، حتى لو كان ذلك من أجل شيء أبدي.

عندما كنت في مشاة البحرية، كانوا يذكروننا باستمرار أن حياتنا ليست رقم واحد؛ وطننا هو. هناك كثير من الشباب الذين يضعون وطنهم أولًا. كثيرون ذهبوا وبذلوا كل ما لديهم؛ كثيرون ماتوا.

في الحرب العالمية الثانية، كان اليابانيون يحاولون التسلل إلى حفر ثعلب تسكنها جنود ويقذفون قنبلة يدوية فيها. كثيرًا ما لم تنتهِ كما أراد اليابانيون، لأن أحدهم يقفز على القنبلة، فيمتص الانفجار. آلاف قدموا حياتهم لينقذوا أصدقائهم ويدافعوا عن وطنهم. لكن تأكد، لو لم تكن أولوياتهم مرتبة (الأمة قبل النفس)، لما فعلوا ذلك.

لو خاطر أحد اليوم، في أمريكا، بحياته من أجل الإنجيل، لصنّفه الناس أنه أحمق ومتهور وغير ناضج. لكن ماذا نقول عن كثيرين من قبلنا—أولئك الذين قدموا حياتهم وهم يدافعون عن نفس الأشياء التي نقول أننا نؤمن بها اليوم؟ وماذا عن الآلاف اليوم الذين يضعون حياتهم على المحك في دول أخرى—هل هم حمقى؟ لننظر إلى مثال واضح جدًا في أعمال الرسل.

وأثناء اقامتنا هناك أيامًا عدة نزل من اليهودية نبي اسمه أغابوس. فلما جاء إلى عندنا أخذ حزام بولس ووثب بيديه ورجليه وقال: هكذا يقول الروح القدس: هكذا يربط يهود أورشليم هذا الرجل الذي له هذا الحزام، ويسلمونه إلى الأمم. فلما سمعنا ذلك توسّلنا نحن والساكنون هناك إليه ألا يصعد إلى أورشليم. فقال بولس: ماذا تريدون أن تبكون وتكسروا قلبي؟ لأني مستعد لا أن أكون مربوطًا فقط بل وموتًا أيضًا في أورشليم من أجل اسم الرب يسوع.—أعمال 21:10-13.

ما رأينا في أفعال بولس اليوم؟ صعد بولس إلى أورشليم فأسرعوا وأخذوه وصُفع وسُجن. كان ذلك بداية النهاية لأخينا العزيز. نُقِل من سجن إلى سجن وانتهى به المطاف في روما حيث قُطع رأسه. ماذا تعتقد أن الذين حاولوا أن يردّوه عن الصعود إلى أورشليم قالوا؟ هل تصوروهم يسمونه أحمق؟ هل هزّوا رؤوسهم وقالوا: «قلت له ألا يذهب!»؟

لا يمكننا أن نعرف يقينًا. ومع ذلك، أنا متأكد أن بولس كان يضع ملكوت المسيح أولًا؛ حياته لم تكن مهمة. كان يطيع الله، وكان الله قد أمره أن يذهب.

حين نحب حياتنا، يصبح من الصعب جدًا أن نكون تلاميذًا فعالين للرب يسوع. ننتهي بالتخلي عن دعوة الله ثم نجد أنفسنا نحاول أن نعيش الحياة المسيحية بمفردنا، وبدون الله—لا عون روحي من فوق، مما يجعلنا نقصر كثيرًا عن المقياس.

من المفارقات أنه فقط عندما نترك كل شيء، بما في ذلك حياتنا، سنجد السلام الحقيقي والهدف لحياتنا. وعندما نحب حياتنا، ففي ذلك الوقت سنفقدها.

توقفوا عن الأمور الهافطة.
أعطوا القلب والروح والفكر والقوة
لخدمة ملك الملوك.

قُوموا، يا قديسي الله!
المملكة تتأخر طويلًا.
أتو بدًا يوم المحبة المشيَّة على مثال المسيح
وأنهِوا ليلة الظلم.

ارفعوا عاليًا صليب المسيح!
اقطَعوا حيث خطا قدمه.
بقيادة ابن الإنسان إلى الأمام،
قُوموا، يا قديسي الله!

لنقم، كشعب الله، ولننتهِ من الأمور الصغرى، ولنوجه نظرنا إلى الأمور العليا، لا إلى أمور هذه الأرض. نعم، سنبرز؛ سيلصقون بنا لقب الحمقى وأشياء كثيرة أخرى. ومع ذلك، سنجذب انتباه الله مرة أخرى وستشتعل نيران الإحياء من جديد!
